description: Ratio of electrical energy output to thermal energy input from nuclear fission, expressed as percentage. Typical nuclear plant thermal efficiency is 33-37%.
reference: ASME Performance Test Code PTC 46 - Overall Plant Performance

description: Primary key for plant

Foreign key linking to asset.registry. Business justification: Asset Management requires each generation plant to be linked to its asset record for depreciation, capital accounting, and maintenance planning.

Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Required for the Balancing Area Settlement Report that allocates each plant's generation to its BA for LMP calculation and regulatory compliance (FERC, NERC).
Foreign key linking to finance.chart_of_accounts. Business justification: Needed for posting plant capital expenditures to the correct GL account in the Capital Projects financial statements.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Required for plant-level cost allocation in the Cost Center Allocation report, enabling O&M expense tracking per plant.
Foreign key linking to workforce.employee. Business justification: Required for Plant Operations Management reports that identify the employee responsible for each plant's compliance and performance.

Foreign key linking to property.parcel. Business justification: Regulatory Asset Registry requires each plant’s land parcel for tax and compliance reporting; linking plant to parcel enables automated reporting to FERC and local authorities.

Foreign key linking to product.rate_schedule. Business justification: Wholesale Power Sales Rate Schedule Assignment links each plant to the rate schedule governing its electricity sales, required for settlement and FERC reporting.

Foreign key linking to technology.scada_system. Business justification: Required for Plant Real‑Time Monitoring & Control; SCADA system ID needed for operational dashboards and NERC CIP compliance reporting.
Foreign key linking to transmission.line. Business justification: Needed for Primary Interconnection Line assignment used in transmission capacity studies and NERC reporting.

Foreign key linking to transmission.transmission_substation. Business justification: Required for Interconnection Planning Report linking each plant to its substation for reliability and regulatory filings.
Actual date when the generation plant was permanently retired from service. Null if plant is still operational.
NERC-registered balancing authority responsible for integrating resource plans and maintaining load-interchange-generation balance within its area.
Current net book value of the plant asset in US dollars after accumulated depreciation.
Average capacity factor as a percentage, representing the ratio of actual energy output to maximum possible output over a reporting period.
City where the generation plant is located.
Indicates whether the plant is a combined heat and power (CHP) facility producing both electricity and useful thermal energy.
Date when the generation plant began commercial operation and started delivering power to the grid.
Total capital expenditure for plant construction in US dollars, used for depreciation and rate base calculations.
Type of cooling system employed by the plant for thermal management.
reference: EIA-860, EPA Cooling Water Intake Structures Rule

description: Three-letter ISO country code where the generation plant is located.
County or equivalent administrative division where the plant is located.
Timestamp when the plant record was first created in the system.
EIA-assigned unique plant identifier used for federal energy data reporting and statistical analysis.
24/7 emergency contact telephone number for the plant used for outage coordination and emergency response.
reference: NERC EOP Standards, Internal Emergency Response Plan

description: Indicates whether the plant has emissions control equipment installed (e.g., scrubbers, selective catalytic reduction).
Primary environmental operating permit number issued by EPA or state environmental agency.
reference: EPA Clean Air Act Title V, State Environmental Permits

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) License Number
description: FERC-issued license number for hydroelectric projects or other facilities requiring federal authorization.

Primary fuel or energy source used by the generation plant for electricity production. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: coal|natural_gas|oil|nuclear|solar|wind|hydro|biomass|geothermal|other — 10 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]

business_glossary_term: Heat Rate British Thermal Units (BTU) per Kilowatt-Hour (kWh)
description: Average heat rate of the plant in BTU per kWh, measuring thermal efficiency of fuel-to-electricity conversion. Lower values indicate higher efficiency.
Total nameplate generation capacity of the plant in megawatts, representing the maximum rated output under ideal conditions.
Voltage level in kilovolts at which the plant interconnects to the transmission grid.

business_glossary_term: Independent System Operator (ISO) or Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) Market
description: Name of the ISO or RTO market where the plant is interconnected and participates in wholesale energy markets.
Timestamp when the plant record was last updated in the system.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the plant location in decimal degrees.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the plant location in decimal degrees.
Name of the individual responsible for day-to-day operations and management of the generation facility.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Plant Code
description: NERC-assigned unique identifier for the generation plant used for reliability reporting and compliance.
Net generation capacity in megawatts after accounting for auxiliary load and station service requirements.
reference: EIA-860, NERC Generating Availability Data System (GADS)

description: Total count of individual generation units or turbines within the plant facility.
Current operational state of the generation plant indicating its availability and readiness to generate power.
Classification of the utility's ownership or contractual relationship with the generation plant.
Primary contact telephone number for the generation plant facility.
Scheduled date for permanent retirement or decommissioning of the generation facility. Null if no retirement is planned.
Internal utility-assigned alphanumeric code for the generation plant used in operational systems.
Official name of the generation facility as registered with regulatory authorities.
Primary classification of the generation facility based on the dominant generation technology employed.
Postal or ZIP code for the plant location.
Specific generation technology employed by the plant (e.g., combined cycle, steam turbine, photovoltaic, wind turbine).
Primary regulatory authority governing the plant operations, typically state Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Public Service Commission (PSC).
Indicates whether the plant is eligible to generate Renewable Energy Certificates under applicable renewable portfolio standards.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System Tag
description: Primary SCADA system tag or identifier used to retrieve real-time operational data from OSIsoft PI Historian.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian, Internal SCADA Standards

description: Two-letter state or province code where the generation plant is located.
Physical street address of the generation plant facility.
Entity that owns the transmission facilities to which the plant is interconnected.
Primary water source used for cooling or steam generation at the plant (e.g., river, lake, ocean, cooling tower).
reference: EPA Clean Water Act Section 316(b), EIA-860

description: Unique identifier for the renewable generation resource. Primary key for the renewable resource master record.

Foreign key linking to customer.customer_account. Business justification: Community‑solar or renewable subscription links a renewable resource record to the subscribing customer account for allocation and reporting.

Foreign key linking to generation.plant. Business justification: Renewable resources are owned by a specific plant; linking provides plant-level aggregation and removes the siloed status of renewable_resource.

Foreign key linking to product.product_program. Business justification: Renewable Incentive Program enrollment tracks each renewable resource's participation in state RPS or incentive programs, needed for compliance reporting.
Foreign key linking to metering.meter. Business justification: Renewable resource (e.g., solar farm) must be linked to a meter for REC tracking and net‑metering calculations.
Foreign key linking to transmission.interconnection_agreement. Business justification: Renewable projects must be linked to their Interconnection Agreement for compliance and market eligibility.

Design or expected capacity factor as a percentage, representing the ratio of actual energy output to theoretical maximum output over a year. Used for Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) modeling and Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) analysis. Typical values: solar 15-25%, wind 30-45%, hydro 40-60%.
reference: IRP Modeling Standards; NREL Annual Technology Baseline

description: Date when the renewable resource achieved commercial operation and began delivering energy under commercial terms. May differ from interconnection date due to testing and commissioning periods. Critical for Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) milestone tracking and Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) eligibility.
reference: EIA Form 860 - Generator Data; PPA Contract Terms

description: Timestamp when this renewable resource record was first created in the system. Used for data lineage and audit trail.
Name of the source system from which this renewable resource record originated (e.g., 'Maximo', 'GIS', 'PI Historian', 'Manual Entry'). Used for data lineage and integration troubleshooting.

business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resource Management System (DERMS) Integration Flag
description: Indicates whether the renewable resource is integrated with the utility's Distributed Energy Resource Management System for real-time monitoring, forecasting, and dispatch control. True if integrated, False otherwise. Supports Virtual Power Plant (VPP) operations and grid flexibility.
reference: IEEE 2030.5 - Smart Energy Profile; DERMS Functional Requirements

description: Unique identifier linking this renewable resource to its asset record in the Enterprise Asset Management system (Maximo). Used for maintenance planning, work order management, and asset lifecycle tracking.

Expected operational lifespan of the renewable resource in years, used for depreciation calculations and long-term resource planning. Typical values: solar 25-30 years, wind 20-25 years, hydro 50-100 years.
reference: FERC Depreciation Guidelines; IRP Planning Assumptions

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts code for capitalization and depreciation of this renewable generation asset. Typically 334 (Solar), 335 (Wind), 331-333 (Hydro) depending on resource type.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts for Electric Utilities

description: Unique identifier linking this renewable resource to its representation in the utility's GIS system (Esri ArcGIS). Enables spatial analysis, asset visualization, and integration with transmission and distribution network models.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Asset Management Data Model

description: Height of the wind turbine hub above ground level in meters. Critical parameter for wind resource assessment and energy yield modeling. Applicable to wind resources only. Null for solar and hydro.

Date when the renewable resource was placed into service for accounting and depreciation purposes. May differ from commercial operation date due to accounting policy. Used for fixed asset management and regulatory rate base calculations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980

description: Nameplate capacity of the renewable resource in megawatts AC (alternating current), representing the maximum continuous electrical output at the point of interconnection. For solar, this is the inverter-limited AC capacity.
reference: FERC Form 1 - Electric Plant in Service; EIA Form 860

description: For solar PV resources, the total DC capacity of the solar panels before inversion. Null for non-solar resources. Used to calculate DC-to-AC ratio for solar performance analysis.
Date when the renewable resource was first interconnected to the grid and authorized to deliver energy. Used for depreciation schedules, regulatory reporting, and capacity factor analysis.
reference: FERC Form 1 - Electric Plant in Service

description: Manufacturer of the inverter equipment for solar PV resources (e.g., 'SMA', 'Fronius', 'SolarEdge'). Applicable to solar PV only. Null for wind and hydro.
Model designation of the inverter equipment for solar PV resources. Applicable to solar PV only. Null for wind and hydro.
Geographic latitude coordinate of the renewable resource location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, wind resource assessment, and transmission planning.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the renewable resource location in decimal degrees. Used for GIS mapping, solar irradiance modeling, wind resource assessment, and transmission planning.
User ID or system account that last modified this renewable resource record. Used for audit trail and data stewardship accountability.
Timestamp when this renewable resource record was last modified. Used for data lineage, change tracking, and audit trail.

Indicates whether the renewable resource is eligible for Net Energy Metering programs, allowing bidirectional energy flow and credit for excess generation. True if eligible, False otherwise. Primarily applicable to distributed solar resources.
reference: State Public Utility Commission NEM Tariffs

description: Current lifecycle status of the renewable resource. In-service indicates active generation capability, standby indicates ready but not generating, out-of-service indicates temporary unavailability, under construction for assets not yet commissioned, retired for permanently decommissioned, mothballed for long-term suspension.

Classification of ownership and operational responsibility. Utility-owned indicates direct ownership and operation, third-party PPA indicates independent power producer with power purchase agreement, customer-owned NEM indicates behind-the-meter distributed generation, joint venture indicates shared ownership.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Internal Ownership Policy

description: Manufacturer and model designation of solar panels installed (e.g., 'SunPower Maxeon 3-400W'). Applicable to solar PV resources only. Null for wind and hydro.

Tag prefix used in OSIsoft PI Historian for real-time telemetry data streams from this renewable resource. Enables linkage between master data and operational time-series data for performance monitoring and analytics.

Unique identifier for the Power Purchase Agreement governing the sale of energy and/or capacity from this renewable resource. References the contractual terms, pricing structure, and delivery obligations. Confidential business information.
reference: FERC Electric Quarterly Report (EQR); Contract Management System

business_glossary_term: Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) Tracking System ID
description: Unique identifier assigned by the regional REC tracking system (e.g., PJM-GATS, WREGIS, M-RETS) for tracking and trading renewable energy certificates generated by this resource. Used for renewable portfolio standard (RPS) compliance and REC monetization.
reference: Regional REC Tracking System Standards (WREGIS, M-RETS, PJM-GATS)

description: Indicates whether this renewable resource record is currently active in the system. True for active records, False for logically deleted or archived records. Used for soft-delete pattern and historical record retention.
Total storage capacity of the hydro reservoir in acre-feet. Applicable to pumped storage and reservoir-based hydro. Null for run-of-river hydro, solar, and wind.
Externally-known unique business identifier for the renewable resource, used in operational systems and regulatory reporting. Typically follows utility naming convention for generation assets.
reference: FERC Form 1 - Electric Plant in Service

description: Human-readable name of the renewable generation resource (e.g., 'Sunrise Solar Farm Unit 1', 'Coastal Wind Turbine 12').
Classification of the renewable generation technology. Solar PV (photovoltaic), solar thermal (concentrating solar power), wind onshore, wind offshore, run-of-river hydro, or pumped storage hydro.
Geographic or operational zone designation for the renewable resource, used for resource planning and dispatch optimization. May align with ISO/RTO pricing zones or internal planning regions.
reference: Internal Resource Planning Standard; ISO/RTO Zone Definitions

description: Date when the renewable resource was permanently retired from service. Null for active resources. Used for asset lifecycle tracking and regulatory reporting.
Diameter of the wind turbine rotor (blade tip to blade tip) in meters. Determines swept area and energy capture capability. Applicable to wind resources only. Null for solar and hydro.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Integration Flag
description: Indicates whether the renewable resource is integrated with the utility's SCADA system for real-time telemetry, monitoring, and control. True if integrated, False otherwise. Supports grid operations and outage management.
reference: NERC CIP Standards; SCADA System Architecture

description: Manufacturer and model designation of wind turbine (e.g., 'GE 2.5-120', 'Vestas V150-4.2MW'). Applicable to wind resources only. Null for solar and hydro.

Vertical distance (head) between the upstream water level and the turbine in meters. Key parameter for hydro generation capacity and efficiency. Applicable to hydro resources only. Null for solar and wind.
Unique surrogate identifier for the balancing authority area (BAA) record in the lakehouse silver layer. Primary key for this master resource entity.
reference: NERC Glossary of Terms; FERC Order 888

description: Short-form abbreviation or acronym for the balancing authority area used in SCADA displays, EMS dispatch screens, and operational communications (e.g., MISO, PJM, SPP).
reference: NERC Glossary of Terms; GE PowerOn Advanced EMS

description: Indicates whether Automatic Generation Control (AGC) is active for this balancing area. AGC continuously adjusts generator output to maintain ACE within NERC BAL-001 limits. Critical flag for EMS dispatch configuration.
reference: NERC BAL-001-2; GE PowerOn Advanced EMS

description: Total geographic area of the balancing authority service territory in square miles. Used in infrastructure density analysis, storm response planning, and regulatory filings with state PUCs.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; State PUC Rate Case Filings

description: Classification of the operational jurisdiction type. Distinguishes between a full NERC-registered balancing authority, a sub-control area operating under a parent BA, or a reserve sharing group. Drives dispatch logic and reliability obligation scope in the EMS.
Full legal or operational name of the balancing authority area as registered with NERC and recognized by FERC. Used in regulatory filings, RTO/ISO coordination, and operational reporting.
reference: NERC Glossary of Terms; FERC Order 888

description: NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) impact classification for this balancing area as a bulk electric system (BES) cyber system. Drives cybersecurity control requirements under NERC CIP-002 through CIP-014 standards.
reference: NERC CIP-002-5.1a; NERC CIP-003-8; FERC Order 822

description: The maximum allowable Area Control Error (ACE) in megawatts for this balancing area, as defined in the NERC BAL-001 standard. ACE is the real-time difference between actual and scheduled interchange plus frequency bias. This limit drives EMS automatic generation control (AGC) setpoints.
reference: NERC BAL-001-2; GE PowerOn Advanced EMS

description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code for the primary country in which this balancing area operates (e.g., USA, CAN, MEX). Relevant for cross-border balancing areas and NERC international coordination.

The timestamp when this balancing area master record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Supports data lineage, audit trail, and regulatory record retention requirements.
reference: FASB ASC 980; NERC Rules of Procedure; ISO 55000

description: Total enrolled demand response (DR) capacity in megawatts (MW) available within this balancing area for dispatch during peak demand or grid emergency events. Includes both direct load control and interruptible load programs.
reference: FERC Order 745; NERC BAL-002-3; DOE DR Program Guidelines

description: Total nameplate capacity of distributed energy resources (DER) — including rooftop solar, battery storage, and small-scale generation — interconnected within this balancing area. Used in DERMS integration and load forecasting.
reference: FERC Order 2222; NERC TPL-001-4; DOE DERMS Guidelines

description: The date on which this balancing area record became operationally effective, including any boundary changes, restructuring events, or RTO/ISO membership transitions. Supports temporal analysis of balancing area configuration history.

business_glossary_term: Energy Information Administration (EIA) Balancing Authority Code
description: The EIA-assigned balancing authority code used in mandatory EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) and EIA Form 411 submissions. Enables linkage between operational data and public EIA reporting.
reference: EIA Form 930; EIA Form 411; DOE Reporting Requirements

description: The native identifier for this balancing area as configured in the GE PowerOn Advanced Energy Management System (EMS). Used for cross-referencing real-time operational data from the EMS with the lakehouse silver layer record.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced EMS; OSIsoft PI Historian

description: The date on which this balancing area record ceases to be effective, typically due to decommissioning, merger with another balancing authority, or transfer of operational control. Null for currently active areas.

The frequency bias setting for this balancing area expressed in megawatts per hertz (MW/Hz). This value is used in the ACE calculation formula and must be reported to NERC annually under BAL-003. Configured in the EMS AGC module.
reference: NERC BAL-003-1.1; GE PowerOn Advanced EMS

description: Descriptive geographic region or service territory description for the balancing area (e.g., Midwest, Pacific Northwest, Southeast). Used for operational reporting, regulatory filings, and GIS-based analysis in Esri ArcGIS.

Total nameplate installed generation capacity in megawatts (MW) within the balancing area boundary. Represents the principal quantitative measure of the resource and is used in IRP filings, NERC reliability assessments, and reserve margin calculations.
reference: NERC TPL-001-4; EIA Form 860; FERC Order 888

description: The method used to schedule energy interchange transactions across the balancing area boundary. E-Tag indicates use of the NERC e-Tag system for electronic tagging of interchange. RTO-managed indicates the RTO/ISO controls interchange scheduling.
reference: NERC INT-001-3; NERC INT-004-3.1; FERC Order 888

description: The North American AC synchronous interconnection to which this balancing area belongs. Determines frequency regulation obligations, emergency assistance protocols, and NERC reliability standards applicability.
reference: NERC Glossary of Terms; EIA Form 411

description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this balancing area master record, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, data quality monitoring, and incremental lakehouse processing.
reference: FASB ASC 980; NERC Rules of Procedure; ISO 55000

description: Decimal latitude of the geographic centroid of the balancing area boundary polygon, in WGS84 coordinate reference system. Used for GIS visualization in Esri ArcGIS and spatial analytics.

business_glossary_term: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) Pricing Node Code
description: The RTO/ISO-assigned pricing node code for the primary Locational Marginal Price (LMP) settlement point associated with this balancing area. Used in Allegro ETRM for energy trading settlement and DAM/RTM position management.
reference: FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Tariff; Allegro ETRM

description: Number of load serving entities (LSEs) operating within this balancing area. Used in resource adequacy planning, reserve sharing agreements, and NERC reliability assessments.
reference: NERC BAL-002-3; FERC Order 888; State PUC Filings

description: Decimal longitude of the geographic centroid of the balancing area boundary polygon, in WGS84 coordinate reference system. Used for GIS visualization in Esri ArcGIS and spatial analytics.

Indicates whether this balancing area participates in a wholesale energy market (Day-Ahead Market or Real-Time Market) operated by an RTO/ISO. True for market-participating areas; False for vertically integrated utilities operating outside organized markets.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 2000; Allegro ETRM

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Balancing Authority Area (BAA) Code
description: The official NERC-assigned alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this balancing authority area within the North American bulk electric system. Used in NERC compliance filings, EIA-411 submissions, and interchange scheduling.
reference: NERC BAL-001-2; EIA Form 411; FERC Order 888

description: The date on which this balancing authority area was formally registered with NERC as a functional entity. Establishes the start of NERC reliability standard compliance obligations.
reference: NERC Rules of Procedure Section 500; NERC BAL-001-2

description: The nominal AC system frequency in hertz (Hz) for this balancing area (typically 60.000 Hz for North American interconnections). Used as the reference frequency for ACE calculations and frequency regulation compliance.
reference: NERC BAL-001-2; NERC BAL-003-1.1; IEEE Std 1547

description: The minimum operating reserve requirement in megawatts (MW) that must be maintained within this balancing area at all times, per NERC BAL-002 and applicable RTO/ISO tariff requirements. Includes both spinning and non-spinning reserves.
reference: NERC BAL-002-3; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Current lifecycle state of the balancing area. Active indicates the area is fully operational and participating in real-time dispatch and frequency regulation. Transitioning indicates a merger, transfer, or restructuring is in progress.

Historical or projected annual peak demand in megawatts (MW) for the balancing area. Used in reserve margin calculations, IRP planning, and NERC reliability assessments submitted to FERC and state PUCs.
reference: NERC TPL-001-4; EIA Form 411; FERC Order 888

description: The primary frequency response obligation assigned to this balancing area, expressed in megahertz (MHz) of frequency deviation response capability. Used in NERC BAL-003 compliance tracking and EMS frequency regulation dispatch.

Total nameplate capacity of renewable energy sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal) in megawatts (MW) within the balancing area. Used in REC tracking, IRP filings, and state renewable portfolio standard (RPS) compliance reporting.
reference: EIA Form 860; State RPS Requirements; FERC Order 888

description: The required or actual planning reserve margin expressed as a percentage of peak load. Represents the buffer of generation capacity above peak demand required to maintain reliability. Reported in IRP filings and NERC assessments.
reference: NERC BAL-002-3; FERC Order 888; State PUC IRP Requirements

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Membership
description: Name of the RTO or ISO within which this balancing area operates or is a member (e.g., PJM Interconnection, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE). Null if the utility operates as an independent balancing authority outside an RTO/ISO.
reference: FERC Order 2000; NERC Glossary of Terms

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Target (Minutes)
description: The annual SAIDI performance target in minutes for this balancing area, representing the average total duration of interruptions per customer. Reported to state PUCs and used in reliability benchmarking.
reference: IEEE Std 1366; State PUC Reliability Standards; NERC Glossary

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Target
description: The annual SAIFI performance target for this balancing area, representing the average number of interruptions per customer per year. Reported to state PUCs and used in reliability benchmarking alongside SAIDI.
reference: IEEE Std 1366; State PUC Reliability Standards; NERC Glossary

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Area Code
description: The SCADA system area code assigned to this balancing area in the operational technology environment. Used to correlate real-time telemetry from OSIsoft PI Historian with the balancing area master record for operational intelligence.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC CIP-007-6

description: The minimum spinning (synchronized) reserve requirement in megawatts (MW) for this balancing area. Spinning reserves must be online and capable of responding within 10 minutes per NERC BAL-002 standards.

Comma-separated list of two-letter US state abbreviations (e.g., OH,IN,MI) representing the states within or overlapping the balancing area boundary. Determines which state PUC jurisdictions apply for rate case filings and regulatory compliance.

Number of high-voltage transmission tie lines connecting this balancing area to adjacent balancing areas. Used in interchange scheduling, contingency analysis, and NERC CIP-014 physical security assessments.
reference: NERC FAC-001-3; NERC FAC-002-3; FERC Order 888

description: The IANA time zone identifier for the primary operating time zone of this balancing area (e.g., America/Chicago, America/New_York). Used for scheduling, dispatch, and market settlement time alignment.
reference: IANA Time Zone Database; NERC INT-001-3

description: The NERC-assigned identifier of the Transmission Operator (TOP) responsible for operating the transmission facilities within this balancing area. May differ from the balancing authority in restructured markets.
reference: NERC TOP-001-4; NERC FAC-001-3; FERC Order 888

description: The primary bulk electric system transmission voltage level in kilovolts (kV) for this balancing area (e.g., 345 kV, 500 kV, 765 kV). Defines the BES threshold and NERC CIP applicability scope.
reference: NERC CIP-002-5.1a; NERC FAC-001-3; FERC Order 888

description: Primary key for control_center
Self-referencing FK on control_center (backup_control_center_id)
Street address of the control center facility.
Maximum generation or load handling capacity in megawatts.
City where the control center is located.
External code used to reference the control center in operational systems.
Primary email address for the control center contact point.
Primary telephone number for the control center contact point.
Name of the individual responsible for overall control center management.
Three‑letter ISO country code of the control center location.
Timestamp when the control center record was first created in the data lake.
Name of the source operational system (e.g., SCADA, EMS) that provides data for this record.
Date the control center was retired or decommissioned (null if still active).
Free‑form description of the control center's purpose and capabilities.
Date the control center became operational.
Electrical grid area or balancing authority the control center serves.
Indicates whether the control center is designated as critical for grid reliability.
Timestamp of the most recent maintenance activity.
Geographic latitude of the control center (decimal degrees).
Geographic longitude of the control center (decimal degrees).
Planned interval in days between routine maintenance events.
Human‑readable name of the control center.
Mode in which the control center operates.
Organization or business unit responsible for operating the control center.
Internal code representing the geographic or operational region.
State or province of the control center location.
Current operational status of the control center.
IANA timezone identifier for the control center location.
Category of control center (e.g., primary, regional, backup).
Timestamp of the most recent update to the control center record.
Nominal voltage level served by the control center.
Postal/ZIP code for the control center address.
Unique surrogate identifier for the electrical control zone record within the balancing area. Primary key for this entity.
reference: NERC Reliability Standards; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Control zones belong to a balancing area; adding balancing_area_id creates proper hierarchy and removes redundant code column.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.cip_standard. Business justification: Each control zone is subject to a specific CIP standard; the FK supports compliance tracking and audit readiness.

Foreign key linking to gridops.control_center. Business justification: A control center oversees multiple control zones; adding control_zone.control_center_id creates the necessary parent relationship and eliminates the silo for control_center.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System Zone ID
description: Zone identifier as registered in the SCADA system (OSIsoft PI Historian / GE PowerOn). Used to correlate real-time telemetry data streams, alarm points, and control actions to this logical control zone.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC CIP-007

description: Number of Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) smart meters deployed within this control zone. Used for demand response targeting, load disaggregation, and meter data management (MDM) reporting.
reference: Oracle Utilities MDM; NIST Smart Grid Framework; EIA Form 861

description: Maximum allowable Area Control Error (ACE) in Megawatts (MW) for this control zone before corrective dispatch action is triggered. Defined per NERC BAL-001 compliance requirements for balancing authority performance.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO Operating Procedures

description: Number of electrical buses (nodes) within this control zone as modeled in the EMS network topology. Used for state estimation, power flow analysis, and contingency analysis.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC MOD-032; IEEE 30-Bus Standard

description: Timestamp when this control zone record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and regulatory record retention requirements.
reference: NERC CIP-007; FASB ASC 980; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: Indicates whether this control zone contains or serves Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) assets as defined by NERC CIP standards. Zones flagged true require enhanced cybersecurity controls and physical security measures.
reference: NERC CIP-002; NERC CIP-007; DHS Critical Infrastructure Framework

description: Total number of end-use customers (residential and commercial) served within this control zone. Used for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reliability index calculations and outage impact assessments.
reference: State PUC Reliability Reporting; EIA Form 861; NERC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: Distributed Energy Resources (DER) Integration Enabled Flag
description: Indicates whether Distributed Energy Resources (DER) — including rooftop solar, battery storage, and small-scale generation — are actively managed within this control zone via the DERMS platform.
reference: FERC Order 2222; IEEE 1547; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: Numeric priority rank assigned to this control zone for load dispatch and restoration sequencing. Lower values indicate higher priority. Used by EMS/DMS operators during contingency events and load shedding scenarios.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-001; State PUC Emergency Operating Procedures

description: Zone identifier as configured in the Distribution Management System (DMS) for feeder switching, fault isolation, and service restoration coordination. Distinct from the EMS zone ID as DMS operates at distribution voltage levels.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; IEEE 1547; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: Indicates whether this control zone participates in Demand Response (DR) dispatch programs. Zones flagged true are included in DR event targeting, load curtailment calculations, and DERMS coordination.
reference: FERC Order 745; State PUC DR Programs; NERC BAL-002

description: Date on which this control zone became operationally active and was formally recognized in the EMS/DMS configuration. Used for regulatory reporting, rate case filings, and historical grid topology analysis.
reference: FERC Form 714; State PUC Filings; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Zone identifier as configured in the Energy Management System (EMS) for state estimation, optimal power flow, and automatic generation control (AGC) dispatch. Enables cross-system traceability between the EMS and the data lakehouse.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC EOP-001; FERC Form 714

description: Number of distribution feeders managed within this control zone. Supports feeder load balancing, switching order management, and outage restoration planning in the DMS.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; Esri ArcGIS; NERC FAC-002

description: Indicates whether this control zone is eligible to provide frequency regulation ancillary services to the balancing authority or RTO/ISO market. True if the zone has resources capable of automatic generation control (AGC) response.
reference: NERC BAL-003; FERC Order 755; RTO/ISO Tariff

description: Name or code of the geographic service territory region in which this control zone is located. Used for regional load forecasting, regulatory reporting to state PUCs, and operational area assignment.
reference: State PUC Service Territory Filings; FERC Form 714; EIA Form 861

description: Zone identifier in the Esri ArcGIS geospatial system. Links the logical control zone to its physical geographic boundary polygon for spatial analysis, outage impact mapping, and infrastructure planning.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; NIST Smart Grid Framework; NERC FAC-002

description: Total installed generation capacity in Megawatts (MW) within or directly serving this control zone. Supports resource adequacy assessments and capacity reserve margin calculations.
reference: NERC MOD-031; FERC Form 860; EIA Form 860

description: North American electrical interconnection to which this control zone belongs: Eastern Interconnection, Western Interconnection, ERCOT (Texas), Alaska, or Hawaii. Determines synchronous grid boundaries and applicable NERC reliability standards.
reference: NERC Reliability Standards; FERC Order 888; EIA Form 411

description: Date of the most recent formal review of this control zone's EMS/DMS configuration parameters, including voltage setpoints, protection relay settings, and dispatch parameters. Supports NERC FAC-002 compliance documentation.
reference: NERC FAC-002; NERC CIP-010; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Type of load forecasting methodology applied to this control zone within the Energy Management System (EMS). Determines how short-term and long-term load forecasts are generated for dispatch coordination and resource planning.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC MOD-032

description: Indicates whether this control zone is eligible for controlled load shedding during grid emergency conditions. Zones containing critical infrastructure (hospitals, emergency services) are typically excluded.
reference: NERC EOP-001; NERC EOP-002; State PUC Emergency Operating Procedures

business_glossary_term: NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Impact Classification
description: NERC CIP impact classification level for Bulk Electric System (BES) assets within this control zone. High and Medium classifications require mandatory cybersecurity and physical security controls per NERC CIP-002 through CIP-014.
reference: NERC CIP-002; NERC CIP-003; NERC CIP-014

description: Indicates whether customers within this control zone are eligible for Net Energy Metering (NEM) programs, allowing bi-directional energy flow credit for distributed generation (e.g., rooftop solar). Affects load forecasting and grid hosting capacity analysis.
reference: State PUC NEM Tariffs; FERC Order 2222; IEEE 1547

description: Zone identifier as registered in the Outage Management System (OMS). Used to correlate outage events, crew dispatch, and restoration activities to this control zone for SAIDI/SAIFI/CAIDI reporting.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; State PUC Outage Reporting; IEEE 1366

description: Maximum recorded or rated peak electrical load in Megawatts (MW) for this control zone. Used as the principal capacity measure for load forecasting, resource adequacy planning, and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) filings.
reference: NERC MOD-031; FERC Form 714; EIA Form 411

description: Minimum required planning reserve margin percentage for this control zone as mandated by the applicable RTO/ISO or state Public Utility Commission (PUC). Expressed as a percentage of peak load.
reference: NERC MOD-031; State PUC Reliability Standards; FERC Order 888

description: Date on which this control zone was retired or decommissioned from active grid operations. Null for currently active zones. Used for historical topology reconstruction and regulatory asset base (RAB) tracking.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management; FERC Form 714; State PUC Filings

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market in which this control zone participates for energy dispatch, ancillary services, and Locational Marginal Price (LMP) settlement.
reference: FERC Order 2000; NERC Reliability Standards; EIA Form 714

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) Target (Minutes)
description: Target System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI) in minutes for this control zone as established in the utility's reliability performance plan or state PUC reliability standards. Benchmarks operational reliability performance.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC Reliability Standards; NERC Reliability Standards

business_glossary_term: System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) Target
description: Target System Average Interruption Frequency Index (SAIFI) — average number of interruptions per customer per year — for this control zone as defined in the utility's reliability plan or state PUC requirements.
reference: IEEE 1366; State PUC Reliability Standards; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Two-letter US state code for the primary jurisdiction in which this control zone operates. Determines applicable state Public Utility Commission (PUC) regulations, rate cases, and reliability standards.
reference: State PUC Regulations; FERC Jurisdictional Filings; EIA Form 861

description: Number of substations included within this control zone. Used for operational complexity assessment, maintenance planning, and regulatory asset base (RAB) reporting.
reference: Esri ArcGIS; Maximo EAM; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Total rated transfer capacity in Megawatts (MW) of all tie lines connecting this control zone to adjacent zones or balancing areas. Used for interchange scheduling and Available Transfer Capability (ATC) calculations.
reference: NERC FAC-012; FERC Order 888; NERC MOD-028

description: Indicates whether Time-of-Use (TOU) pricing rates are applicable to customers within this control zone. Drives load shape modeling and demand response program design for the zone.
reference: State PUC Rate Cases; FERC Order 745; Oracle CC&B CIS

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this control zone record in the data lakehouse. Used for change data capture (CDC), incremental processing, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: NERC CIP-007; FASB ASC 980; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: Operational mode for voltage control within this zone as configured in the DMS/EMS. Automatic mode enables closed-loop voltage regulation; supervisory mode allows operator-directed control; manual mode requires direct field action.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC FAC-002; IEEE 1547

description: Nominal operating voltage level of the control zone in kilovolts (kV). Defines the voltage class for equipment ratings, protection coordination, and voltage control strategy within the zone.
reference: NERC FAC-001; IEEE C57.12; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Code identifying the weather forecast zone associated with this control zone. Weather zone data drives temperature-sensitive load forecasting models and storm preparedness planning within the EMS.
reference: NOAA Weather Zones; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC MOD-032

description: Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the control zone within the Energy Management System (EMS) and Distribution Management System (DMS). Used in SCADA displays, switching orders, and operational reports.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC Reliability Standards; FERC Order 2000

description: Free-text operational description of the control zone including its geographic boundaries, key assets, operational characteristics, and any special operating conditions or constraints relevant to dispatch and reliability management.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Human-readable name of the control zone used in operational dashboards, load forecasting reports, and dispatch coordination communications.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Current lifecycle status of the control zone within the EMS/DMS. Active zones participate in real-time dispatch and load forecasting. Commissioning zones are being brought into service. Decommissioned zones are retired from grid operations.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; NERC Reliability Standards; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Operational classification of the control zone indicating its primary grid function: load (demand-side), generation (supply-side), transmission (bulk power), distribution (end-delivery), balancing (area control), or interchange (tie-point between areas).
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Unique identifier for the grid contingency scenario record. Primary key for the grid contingency data product.
reference: NERC TPL-001-5 Transmission System Planning Performance Requirements

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) System Identifier
description: Identifier of the SCADA system that provides real-time telemetry data for the elements involved in this contingency scenario.
Code identifying the balancing area or balancing authority area where this contingency is defined and monitored, used for jurisdictional and operational coordination.

Assessment of the risk that this contingency could trigger cascading outages affecting a wider area of the Bulk Electric System (BES), based on system topology, protection schemes, and historical events.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Transmission Planning (TPL) Contingency Category
description: NERC TPL planning category classification: P0 (no contingency/base case), P1 (single element), P2 (single element with stuck breaker), P3 (loss of generator), P4 (multiple elements), P5 (delayed fault clearing), P6 (system instability), P7 (common structure). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: P0|P1|P2|P3|P4|P5|P6|P7 — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Unique business identifier or code used to reference this contingency in operational systems, study reports, and inter-system communication.
Human-readable name or label assigned to this contingency scenario for operator identification and reference in Energy Management System (EMS) displays and reports.

Classification of the contingency scenario based on the number and type of elements removed. N-1 represents single element outage, N-2 represents simultaneous loss of two elements, N-1-1 represents sequential loss of two elements. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: N-1|N-2|N-1-1|generator_trip|line_trip|transformer_trip|bus_fault|multiple_element — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: NERC TPL-001-5 Category P1 through P7

description: Boolean flag indicating whether corrective actions (generation redispatch, transmission switching, load shedding) are required to maintain system reliability if this contingency occurs.
Maximum time in minutes allowed to implement corrective actions after this contingency occurs, based on thermal time constants, voltage decay rates, and operational procedures.

Type of corrective action recommended or required to mitigate violations resulting from this contingency. May include multiple actions separated by semicolons (e.g., 'generation redispatch; transmission switching').
Timestamp when this contingency record was first created in the system, supporting audit trail and data lineage requirements.
Identifier linking this contingency to the DMS zone for transmission-distribution coordination and voltage control at the interface.
Date when this contingency definition became active and was included in security assessment processes.

business_glossary_term: Number of Elements Removed in Contingency
description: Count of transmission or generation elements (lines, transformers, generators, buses) that are removed or tripped in this contingency scenario definition.
Identifier of the EMS system instance where this contingency definition is maintained and where real-time security assessments are executed.

Date when this contingency definition expires or is scheduled to be removed from active security assessment, typically due to system topology changes or element retirement. Null for indefinite contingencies.
Geographic region or sub-region identifier for this contingency, used for regional reliability coordination and reporting.

Current lifecycle status of the contingency scenario in the real-time security assessment engine. Active contingencies are monitored continuously; inactive contingencies are excluded from real-time analysis.
North American power grid interconnection where this contingency is located: Eastern Interconnection, Western Interconnection, Texas Interconnection (ERCOT), or Quebec Interconnection.
Timestamp of the most recent real-time or study-mode security assessment execution that evaluated this contingency scenario.
Timestamp when this contingency most recently resulted in a thermal, voltage, or stability violation during security assessment. Null if no violations have been detected.
Total customer load in megawatts that could be interrupted or at risk of interruption if this contingency occurs and results in cascading outages or system instability.
Timestamp when this contingency record was most recently modified, supporting change tracking and audit requirements.

Count of transmission elements (lines, transformers, interfaces) that are monitored for thermal overload, voltage violation, or stability issues when this contingency is applied in security assessment.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Classification
description: NERC CIP impact rating classification for the elements involved in this contingency, indicating the cyber security and physical security requirements applicable to these assets.
reference: NERC CIP-002 BES Cyber System Categorization

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Regional Entity
description: NERC regional entity with reliability oversight for this contingency scenario (e.g., WECC, MRO, NPCC, RF, SERC, Texas RE).
Identifier linking this contingency to the OMS zone for coordination of planned and unplanned outage management and customer impact assessment.
Name or identifier of the primary transmission or generation element that is removed in this contingency scenario, as defined in the EMS network model.
reference: NERC MOD-032 Data for Power System Modeling and Analysis

description: Type classification of the primary element that is removed or fails in this contingency scenario.

business_glossary_term: Primary Element Voltage Level in Kilovolts (kV)
description: Nominal voltage level in kilovolts of the primary element involved in the contingency scenario.
Qualitative assessment of the likelihood of this contingency occurring based on historical outage data, equipment reliability, and operational experience.
Quantitative probability estimate (0.0 to 1.0) representing the annual likelihood of this contingency scenario occurring, derived from historical reliability data and risk assessment models.
reference: IEEE 762 Standard for Definitions for Use in Reporting Electric Generating Unit Reliability

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in the real-time security assessment (RTSA) engine that runs continuously in the EMS to monitor system security.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the RTO or ISO that has operational or planning jurisdiction over this contingency scenario (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP, NYISO, ISO-NE).
Name or identifier of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Null for single-element contingencies.

Type classification of the secondary element removed in N-2 or N-1-1 contingency scenarios. Set to 'none' for single-element (N-1) contingencies. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: transmission_line|transformer|generator|bus|shunt_device|hvdc_link|none — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Assessment of the potential impact severity if this contingency were to occur, considering load at risk, voltage collapse potential, cascading outage risk, and system stability margin degradation.

Percentage margin between the current operating point and the stability limit (voltage collapse point or transient stability limit) under this contingency scenario. Higher values indicate greater system security.
Two-letter state or province code where the primary contingency element is located, used for regulatory reporting and jurisdictional coordination.
Boolean flag indicating whether this contingency is included in offline study-mode security assessments used for day-ahead planning, seasonal studies, and long-term transmission planning.
Maximum thermal capacity in MVA for the most critical monitored element under this contingency scenario, representing the binding constraint for system operations.

business_glossary_term: Lower Voltage Limit in Per Unit (pu)
description: Minimum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 0.90 to 0.95 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.

business_glossary_term: Upper Voltage Limit in Per Unit (pu)
description: Maximum acceptable voltage in per-unit (pu) for monitored buses under this contingency scenario, typically 1.05 to 1.10 pu for transmission systems per NERC standards.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Point ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each SCADA telemetry point in the master catalog. Serves as the primary key for the scada_point product in the Databricks Silver Layer. Entity role: MASTER_RESOURCE — represents a configured telemetry measurement point owned and managed by the utility.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Configuration; NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82 ICS Security

description: Reference to the grid asset (substation, transformer, generator, transmission line, distribution feeder, capacitor bank, etc.) that this SCADA point monitors or controls. Links the telemetry point to the physical asset in the asset management system (Maximo EAM or Esri ArcGIS). Used for asset health analytics and outage correlation.
reference: Maximo EAM Asset Record; Esri ArcGIS Network Feature; IEC 61968/61970 CIM PowerSystemResource; ISO 55000

description: Reference to the grid asset (substation, transformer, generator, transmission line, distribution feeder, capacitor bank, etc.) that this SCADA point monitors or controls. Links the telemetry point to the physical asset in the asset management system (Maximo EAM or Esri ArcGIS). Used for asset health analytics and outage correlation.
reference: Maximo EAM Asset Record; Esri ArcGIS Network Feature; IEC 61968/61970 CIM PowerSystemResource; ISO 55000

description: Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: SCADA points are located within a balancing area; linking provides spatial context and removes string field.

Foreign key linking to technology.it_asset. Business justification: Each SCADA point corresponds to a physical IT asset (sensor/device); linking supports maintenance schedules and regulatory asset tracking.

Foreign key linking to technology.network_device. Business justification: SCADA points are collected via network devices; linking enables IT asset management and cybersecurity compliance for each point.
Foreign key linking to der.der_resource. Business justification: SCADA points monitor DER inverter output for real‑time operations; utility operators need this link for dispatch and compliance.

Reference to the substation or switching station where the field device associated with this SCADA point is physically located. Used for geographic grouping, outage management correlation, and NERC reliability reporting. Links to the substation master record in GIS and EMS network model.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Substation Feature Class; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Network Model; NERC FAC-001; IEC 61968/61970 CIM Substation

business_glossary_term: SCADA Point Critical High Alarm Limit
description: The critical upper threshold (High-High) above which an emergency or critical alarm is triggered, indicating a severe operational condition requiring immediate operator action. Expressed in engineering units. Used in EMS/DMS for two-tier alarm escalation (High vs. High-High). Supports NERC reliability event classification.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Alarm Configuration; NERC EOP-004-3; IEC 61511 Functional Safety

description: The upper operational threshold above which an alarm condition is triggered in the EMS/DMS/SCADA system. When the measured value exceeds this limit, an alarm notification is generated for grid operators. Expressed in engineering units. Configured in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS alarm management module.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Alarm Configuration; NERC EOP-004-3; NERC CIP-007-6; IEC 62351

description: The lower operational threshold below which an alarm condition is triggered in the EMS/DMS/SCADA system. When the measured value falls below this limit, an alarm notification is generated for grid operators. Expressed in engineering units. Configured in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS alarm management module.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Alarm Configuration; NERC EOP-004-3; NERC CIP-007-6; IEC 62351

business_glossary_term: SCADA Point Critical Low Alarm Limit
description: The critical lower threshold (Low-Low) below which an emergency or critical alarm is triggered, indicating a severe operational condition requiring immediate operator action. Expressed in engineering units. Used in EMS/DMS for two-tier alarm escalation (Low vs. Low-Low). Supports NERC reliability event classification.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Alarm Configuration; NERC EOP-004-3; IEC 61511 Functional Safety

description: The operational asset class of the grid infrastructure element monitored by this SCADA point. Used for domain routing, regulatory reporting boundary classification, and T&D cost allocation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|substation|gas_pipeline|gas_distribution|metering|protection — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); NERC BES Definition; IEC 61968/61970 CIM

description: The date on which this SCADA point was formally commissioned and activated in the operational SCADA/EMS/DMS system. Marks the start of the point's active lifecycle. Used for asset age analysis, warranty tracking, and NERC CIP change management audit trails.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management; NERC CIP-010-3 Configuration Change Management; SAP PM Equipment Master

description: The communication protocol used to transmit telemetry data from the field device (RTU/IED) to the SCADA master station for this point. Common utility protocols include DNP3, IEC 60870-5-101/104, IEC 61850, Modbus, and ICCP for inter-control-center communications. Used for cybersecurity classification and NERC CIP asset categorization. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: DNP3|IEC60870-5-101|IEC60870-5-104|Modbus|IEC61850|ICCP|OPC-DA|OPC-UA — promote to reference product]
reference: IEEE 1815 DNP3; IEC 60870-5; IEC 61850; NERC CIP-007-6; NIST SP 800-82 ICS Security

description: Indicates whether OSIsoft PI Historian data compression (exception and compression deviation) is enabled for this point. When True, PI Historian applies the deadband_value and compression deviation to reduce storage while preserving data fidelity. When False, all scanned values are archived (raw storage mode). Impacts PI Historian storage sizing and data retrieval performance.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Compression Settings; OSIsoft PI System Management Tools Documentation

description: The timestamp when this SCADA point record was first created in the master catalog (Silver Layer). Represents the audit creation time in the Databricks Lakehouse. Formatted as yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX per enterprise timestamp convention.
reference: NERC CIP-010-3 Configuration Change Management; NIST SP 800-53 AU-3 Audit Records; ISO 55000

description: The current or last-known data quality status of this SCADA point as reported by OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS. 'good' = valid telemetry; 'bad' = communication failure or device fault; 'uncertain' = questionable signal; 'substituted' = manually overridden value; 'manual_entry' = operator-entered value; 'out_of_range' = value outside raw limits. Used for data quality filtering in analytics.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian System Digital States; IEC 61968/61970 CIM Quality; OPC DA Quality Codes; NERC CIP-007-6

description: The minimum change in the measured value required to trigger a new data archive event in OSIsoft PI Historian (exception deviation). Expressed in the same engineering units as the point. Prevents excessive data storage for slowly-changing signals while ensuring meaningful changes are captured. Configured per point in PI Historian compression settings.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Compression and Exception Settings; NERC FAC-002; EIA Form 411

description: The date on which this SCADA point was decommissioned and removed from active scanning in the SCADA/EMS/DMS system. Null if the point is still active. Used for lifecycle management, historical data archival decisions, and NERC CIP asset retirement documentation.
reference: ISO 55000 Asset Management; NERC CIP-010-3 Configuration Change Management; SAP PM Equipment Master

description: The point address or database key used to reference this telemetry point within the GE PowerOn EMS/DMS real-time database. Typically a hierarchical address string (e.g., 'AREA.SUBSTATION.DEVICE.MEASUREMENT'). Used for EMS state estimation, contingency analysis, and real-time display binding.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Real-Time Database Configuration; IEC 61968/61970 CIM; NERC CIP-007-6

description: Identifies whether this SCADA point monitors an electric grid asset or a natural gas infrastructure asset. 'electric' = electric T&D or generation; 'gas' = natural gas pipeline, compressor, or distribution; 'both' = dual-fuel or combined measurement point. Supports domain partitioning for electric vs. gas operations analytics.
reference: FERC Form 1 (Electric); FERC Form 2 (Gas); PHMSA Gas Distribution Reporting; EIA Form 176

description: The physical unit of measurement associated with the SCADA point value (e.g., 'kV', 'MW', 'MVAr', 'A', 'Hz', 'degF', 'PSI', 'MCF/hr', 'kWh'). Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian engineering unit configuration. Critical for correct interpretation of telemetry values in EMS, DMS, and analytics applications. Aligns with IEC 61970 CIM unit symbols.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Engineering Units; IEC 61970-301 CIM UnitSymbol; IEEE C37.118

description: The SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) functional location code identifying the hierarchical physical location of the asset associated with this SCADA point (e.g., 'TX-SUBST-A-XFMR-01'). Links SCADA telemetry to the SAP ERP asset hierarchy for O&M cost allocation, work order management, and CAPEX/OPEX tracking.
reference: SAP PM Functional Location (IL01); SAP ERP FI/CO Asset Accounting; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: The unique feature identifier from Esri ArcGIS for the network element (substation, line segment, transformer, etc.) associated with this SCADA point. Enables spatial analysis, outage mapping, and geographic visualization of real-time telemetry in the GIS platform. Links SCADA data to the geospatial network model.
reference: Esri ArcGIS Electric Network Feature Dataset; IEC 61968/61970 CIM Geographic; NERC FAC-001

description: Indicates whether alarm processing is enabled for this SCADA point in the EMS/DMS alarm management system. True = alarm limits are active and will generate operator notifications; False = alarm processing suppressed (e.g., during maintenance or commissioning). Drives alarm display filtering in GE PowerOn EMS/DMS.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Alarm Management; NERC EOP-004-3; IEC 62351-7

description: Indicates whether this SCADA point is associated with a Bulk Electric System (BES) element as defined by NERC. BES-applicable points are subject to NERC CIP cybersecurity standards and NERC reliability standards reporting requirements. True = BES applicable; False = non-BES (distribution or sub-transmission).
reference: NERC BES Definition (Effective July 1, 2014); NERC CIP-002-5.1a; FERC Order 773

description: Indicates whether this SCADA point is subject to NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) cybersecurity standards. CIP-applicable points require access control, monitoring, and change management per NERC CIP-007-6. True = CIP applicable; False = not subject to CIP requirements.
reference: NERC CIP-002-5.1a; NERC CIP-007-6; NERC CIP-010-3; NIST SP 800-82

description: Indicates whether this SCADA point supports remote control operations (e.g., breaker open/close, tap changer raise/lower, setpoint adjustment) from the EMS/DMS/SCADA master station. True = remote control enabled; False = read-only telemetry. Critical for access control and NERC CIP classification of control points.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Control Configuration; NERC CIP-007-6; NERC CIP-005-6 Electronic Security Perimeter

description: The date of the most recent calibration or verification of the field instrument (transducer, CT, PT, transmitter) associated with this SCADA point. Used for instrument maintenance scheduling, data quality assurance, and OSHA/PHMSA compliance for gas measurement instruments.
reference: OSHA 29 CFR 1910; PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192/193; NIST Handbook 44; Maximo EAM Calibration Work Order

description: The timestamp when this SCADA point record was most recently updated in the master catalog. Tracks configuration changes to point attributes (alarm limits, scan rate, deadband, etc.). Critical for NERC CIP-010-3 configuration change management audit trail and Silver Layer incremental load processing.
reference: NERC CIP-010-3 Configuration Change Management; NIST SP 800-53 AU-3; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: The physical or electrical quantity being measured by this SCADA point. Categorizes the telemetry by measurement domain for analytics, display grouping, and regulatory reporting. Examples: 'voltage' (kV), 'power_mw' (real power), 'power_mvar' (reactive power), 'frequency' (Hz), 'flow_mcf' (gas flow), 'pressure' (PSI). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: voltage|current|power_mw|power_mvar|frequency|energy_mwh|flow_mcf|pressure|temperature|status_indication|position — promote to reference product]
reference: IEC 61970-301 CIM MeasurementType; IEEE C37.118; EIA Form 411; FERC Form 1

description: The scheduled date for the next calibration or verification of the field instrument associated with this SCADA point. Drives preventive maintenance work order generation in Maximo EAM. Ensures compliance with PHMSA gas measurement calibration intervals and OSHA instrument maintenance requirements.
reference: PHMSA 49 CFR Part 192; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; Maximo EAM PM Schedule; ISO 55000

description: The expected or design nominal operating value for this SCADA point under normal grid conditions (e.g., nominal voltage = 138.0 kV, nominal frequency = 60.0 Hz). Used as a reference baseline for deviation analysis, alarm limit setting, and grid state estimation in EMS. Expressed in engineering units.
reference: GE PowerOn EMS/DMS State Estimation; NERC FAC-001; IEEE C57.12 Transformer Standards

description: Additive offset applied after scale factor conversion to produce the final engineering unit value from the raw telemetry input. Used to correct for zero-point calibration errors or instrument biases. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS as part of the point's conversion formula.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Attributes; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Analog Input Configuration; NIST Handbook 44 Calibration

description: The native point identifier (PI Point ID or PI Tag Name) assigned by OSIsoft PI Historian for this SCADA telemetry point. Used for direct API queries to PI Historian via PI Web API or PI OLEDB. Enables traceability from the Silver Layer back to the source historian record.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Administration; OSIsoft PI Web API; NERC CIP-007-6

description: Functional classification of the SCADA point indicating its operational role. 'measurement' = real-time telemetry value; 'status' = equipment state indication; 'control' = remotely operable control point; 'setpoint' = configurable operating parameter; 'alarm' = alarm/event indicator. Used for access control, display filtering, and NERC CIP classification.
reference: IEC 61968/61970 Common Information Model (CIM); NERC CIP-007-6; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Configuration

description: Free-text description of the SCADA telemetry point providing additional context about what is being measured, the associated equipment, and its operational significance. Sourced from OSIsoft PI Historian point descriptor field. Used in operator displays, engineering documentation, and data catalog search.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Descriptor Attribute; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Point Documentation

description: Human-readable name of the SCADA telemetry point as configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS. Serves as the primary identity label for the point (e.g., 'SUBST_A_BUS1_VOLT', 'GEN_UNIT3_MW_OUTPUT'). Used by grid operators and engineers to identify the measurement in real-time displays and historian queries.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Configuration; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Tag Naming Convention; IEEE C37.118

description: Current lifecycle status of the SCADA point in the master catalog. 'active' = currently scanning and reporting; 'inactive' = configured but not scanning; 'commissioned' = newly added and validated; 'decommissioned' = retired from service; 'suspended' = temporarily halted due to maintenance or fault. Drives data quality filtering in PI Historian and Silver Layer ingestion.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Administration; NERC CIP-007-6 R1; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Classification of the SCADA telemetry point by signal type. 'analog' = continuous measurement (e.g., voltage, MW flow); 'digital' = discrete state (e.g., breaker open/closed); 'accumulator' = pulse-count integration (e.g., energy meter pulse); 'string' = text-based status; 'calculated' = derived value computed within the historian or EMS.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Class Definitions; IEC 61968/61970 CIM; IEEE C37.118.2

description: The maximum raw input value (in engineering units) that the SCADA point can physically receive from the field device before being flagged as out-of-range. Values above this threshold are treated as bad quality data. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS/DMS for data validation.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Attributes; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Limit Configuration; IEC 61968/61970 CIM

description: The minimum raw input value (in engineering units) that the SCADA point can physically receive from the field device before being flagged as out-of-range. Values below this threshold are treated as bad quality data. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS/DMS for data validation.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Attributes; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Limit Configuration; IEC 61968/61970 CIM

description: The communication address of the Remote Terminal Unit (RTU) or Intelligent Electronic Device (IED) from which this SCADA point is polled. Includes protocol-specific addressing (e.g., DNP3 address, Modbus register, IEC 60870-5-101/104 information object address). Used for field device troubleshooting and communication diagnostics.
reference: DNP3 Protocol Standard (IEEE 1815); IEC 60870-5-101/104; NERC CIP-007-6 R1; NIST SP 800-82

description: Multiplier applied to the raw telemetry input value to convert it to engineering units. For example, a current transformer (CT) ratio or potential transformer (PT) ratio applied to raw analog counts. Configured in OSIsoft PI Historian or GE PowerOn EMS/DMS as part of the point's conversion formula.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Point Attributes; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Analog Input Configuration; IEEE C57.13 Instrument Transformers

description: The frequency in seconds at which the SCADA system polls or samples this telemetry point from the field device (RTU, IED, or PLC). Common values: 2 (high-frequency protection), 4 (standard SCADA), 30 (slow telemetry), 60 (non-critical). Determines data density in PI Historian and impacts AMI/SCADA bandwidth planning.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Scan Class Configuration; NERC CIP-007-6; IEEE C37.118.2 Synchrophasor Standard

description: The operational system of record from which this SCADA point configuration originates. Identifies whether the point is mastered in OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn EMS, GE PowerOn DMS, a field RTU/IED, DERMS, or OMS. Critical for data lineage, integration mapping, and Silver Layer ingestion pipeline routing.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS; NERC CIP-007-6 R1; NIST SP 800-82

description: Externally-known unique tag identifier assigned to the SCADA point in the source operational system (OSIsoft PI Historian tag name or GE PowerOn point address). This is the business identifier used across OMS, DMS, EMS, and PI Historian integrations to reference the telemetry point. Equivalent to the PI tag name in OSIsoft PI.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian Tag Naming Standard; GE PowerOn EMS/DMS Configuration; NERC CIP-007-6

description: The nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the electrical bus, equipment, or circuit that this SCADA point is associated with (e.g., 500 kV, 230 kV, 138 kV, 69 kV, 12.47 kV, 0.48 kV). Used for voltage class filtering, T&D boundary classification, and NERC BES (Bulk Electric System) applicability determination.
reference: NERC BES Definition; FERC Order 773; IEC 60038 Standard Voltages; IEEE C57.12

business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Allocation - Switching Order Material Id
description: Primary key for the switching_order_material_allocation association

business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Allocation - Gridops Switching Order Id
description: Foreign key linking to the switching order

business_glossary_term: Switching Order Material Allocation - Material Master Id
description: Foreign key linking to the material master
Current status of the material line (e.g., planned, allocated, released)
Amount of the material allocated to the switching order
Unit of measure for the allocated quantity (e.g., EA, KG)
Unique identifier for the transmission limit record. Primary key for this entity.
Foreign key linking to gridops.balancing_area. Business justification: Transmission limits are defined per balancing area; FK adds relational context.
Name or identifier of the transmission engineer or reliability coordinator who approved this limit for operational use.
Identifier of the transmission facility (line, transformer, flowgate, interface) to which this limit applies.
Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius at which the limit rating was calculated. Used for dynamic rating adjustments.
Date on which this transmission limit was formally approved for enforcement in real-time operations.
Name of the contingency scenario (e.g., N-1, N-2 outage) under which this limit applies. Identifies the specific outage condition that triggers this constraint.
Classification of the contingency: N-1 (single element outage), N-2 (double contingency), base case (no outage), or extreme event.
Timestamp when this transmission limit record was first created in the system.
Indicates whether dynamic line rating (real-time adjustment based on weather and conductor temperature) is enabled for this facility. True if enabled, False otherwise.
Date from which this transmission limit becomes active and enforceable in real-time operations and EMS security analysis.
Short-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 15 minutes without damage, used during contingency conditions.
Long-term emergency rating in MVA that the facility can sustain for up to 4 hours, typically used for post-contingency load relief operations.
Identifier of this limit record in the Energy Management System (EMS) used for real-time security analysis and dispatch.
Date on which this transmission limit expires or is superseded by a new limit. Null if the limit is open-ended.

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Jurisdiction Flag
