description: Indicates whether this transmission facility and its limits fall under FERC jurisdiction (interstate transmission). True if FERC-jurisdictional, False otherwise.
Identifier of the corresponding transmission facility feature in the GIS system, used for geospatial analysis and mapping.
Free-text notes providing additional context, operational instructions, or special conditions related to this transmission limit.
Origin of the limit value: thermal analysis, voltage analysis, stability study, manufacturer equipment rating, field test measurement, or engineering judgment.
Current lifecycle status of the limit record: active (enforced in EMS), inactive, suspended (temporarily not enforced), pending approval, or retired.
Physical constraint type: thermal (conductor heating), voltage (bus voltage deviation), stability (transient/voltage/oscillatory stability limits).
Maximum load that can be shed or transferred through this facility during emergency load dump or load shedding operations.
Timestamp when this transmission limit record was last modified or updated.

business_glossary_term: North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) Classification
description: NERC CIP impact classification of the facility: high, medium, low, or not applicable. Determines cybersecurity and physical security requirements.
Continuous normal operating limit in megavolt-amperes (MVA) under normal ambient and system conditions. This is the baseline thermal or transfer capability limit.
Continuous normal operating limit in megawatts (MW) for real power transfer. Used for flowgates and interfaces where MW is the primary constraint metric.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: Code of the RTO or ISO that has operational authority over this transmission facility and enforces these limits in market operations.

business_glossary_term: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Monitored Flag
description: Indicates whether this transmission limit is actively monitored in real-time via SCADA telemetry. True if monitored, False otherwise.
Season during which this limit applies: summer, winter, spring, fall, or year-round. Seasonal limits reflect ambient temperature and load pattern variations.
Multiplier applied to base ratings to account for seasonal ambient temperature variations (e.g., summer de-rating, winter up-rating). Typically ranges from 0.8 to 1.2.
Reference identifier or document name of the engineering study (thermal, voltage, or stability study) that established this limit.
Nominal voltage level in kilovolts (kV) of the transmission facility (e.g., 138 kV, 230 kV, 345 kV, 500 kV).
Upper voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Exceeding this limit may cause equipment damage or system instability.
Lower voltage limit in kilovolts (kV) for voltage-constrained facilities. Falling below this limit may cause voltage collapse or equipment malfunction.
Primary key for the dispatch_participation association

business_glossary_term: Dispatch Participation - Dr Dispatch Event Id
description: Foreign key linking to dr_dispatch_event
Foreign key linking to meter
Actual MW reduction achieved by the meter during the dispatch event
Status of the meter's participation in the dispatch event (e.g., responded, no‑response)
Timestamp when the meter reported its response to the dispatch event

business_glossary_term: Energy Management System (EMS) Dispatch Instruction ID
description: Unique surrogate identifier for each EMS dispatch instruction record in the balancing area. Primary key for this entity.
Reference to the balancing authority area within which this dispatch instruction is issued. Aligns with NERC balancing area definitions.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888

description: Reference to the pricing node at which the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) applies for this dispatch instruction. Used for economic dispatch optimization and settlement calculations.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO LMP methodology

description: Foreign key linking to der.program. Business justification: EMS dispatch may include specific DER program instructions for ancillary services; operators need the program reference.
Reference to a switching order in the DMS (Distribution Management System) or EMS that is coordinated with this dispatch instruction. Used when dispatch is part of a planned switching sequence.
reference: NERC EOP-001; NERC TOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.
reference: NERC CIP-004; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

description: Reference to the generating unit or controllable resource to which this dispatch instruction is directed. Links to the asset registry in Maximo or GIS.
reference: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 860; FERC Order 888

description: Reference to an associated outage or reliability event in the OMS (Outage Management System) that triggered or is related to this dispatch instruction. Populated for reliability-driven dispatches.
reference: NERC EOP-001; NERC TOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Reference to the EMS operator or system entity (AGC) that issued this dispatch instruction. Used for accountability and audit trail per NERC CIP and reliability standards.
reference: NERC CIP-004; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

description: The SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) telemetry point identifier associated with the generating unit's MW output measurement in OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to correlate dispatch instructions with real-time telemetry data.
reference: NERC CIP-007; OSIsoft PI Historian; NIST SP 800-82

description: Status of the generating unit or resource operator's acknowledgment of this dispatch instruction. Pending indicates awaiting response; acknowledged confirms receipt; not_acknowledged indicates no response within the required window; rejected indicates the resource declined the instruction.
reference: NERC EOP-001; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: The date and time at which the generating unit operator or automated system acknowledged receipt of this dispatch instruction.
reference: NERC EOP-001; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Sequential number assigned by the Automatic Generation Control (AGC) system for this dispatch instruction within a given AGC scan cycle. Used to correlate instructions to AGC telemetry cycles in OSIsoft PI Historian.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; IEEE Std 1547

description: The estimated CO2 emission rate for the dispatched generating unit at the instructed MW setpoint, expressed in pounds per MWh. Used for environmental compliance reporting to EPA and state regulators.
reference: EPA eGRID; EPA Clean Air Act; DOE EIA; FERC Order 888

description: Indicates whether the generating unit complied with this dispatch instruction within the required response time and MW tolerance. True if compliant; False if non-compliant. Used for NERC BAL reliability reporting.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888

description: The name or identifier of the N-1 or N-2 contingency scenario that triggered this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Used for post-contingency analysis and NERC reliability event reporting.
reference: NERC TPL-001; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888

description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was first captured in the Silver Layer data product. Audit trail field for data lineage and regulatory compliance.
reference: NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82; FASB ASC 980

description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Demand Response (DR) resource rather than a traditional generating unit. True when the controllable resource is a DR program participant.
reference: FERC Order 745; NERC BAL-001; DOE DR guidelines

description: Indicates whether this dispatch instruction targets a Distributed Energy Resource (DER) such as rooftop solar, battery storage, or small-scale generation managed via DERMS.
reference: FERC Order 2222; IEEE Std 1547; NERC BAL-001; DOE DERMS guidelines

description: The primary reason for issuing this dispatch instruction. Economic dispatch optimizes cost; reliability dispatch addresses grid stability; regulation dispatch supports frequency control; emergency dispatch responds to contingency events; voltage_support addresses reactive power needs; reserve dispatch activates operating reserves. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: economic|reliability|regulation|emergency|voltage_support|reserve — promote to reference product]
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; NERC EOP-001; FERC Order 888; LMP market rules

description: Indicates whether the dispatch instruction was generated automatically by the AGC system or issued manually by an EMS operator. Automatic instructions originate from AGC scan cycles; manual instructions are operator-initiated.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888

description: The date and time at which the dispatch instruction is expected to take effect at the generating unit. May differ from instruction_timestamp due to ramp lead time or scheduling offset.

The primary energy source type of the dispatched generating unit or resource. Used for generation mix reporting, renewable energy tracking, and REC (Renewable Energy Certificate) accounting. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: fossil_fuel|nuclear|hydro|wind|solar|battery_storage|demand_response|other — promote to reference product]
reference: EIA Form 860; EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; FERC Order 888

description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction expires or is superseded if not acknowledged or executed. After this time, the instruction is considered void.

Indicates whether this dispatch instruction is associated with frequency regulation service (AGC regulation signal). True when the instruction is part of a regulation up/down signal from the balancing authority.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755

description: The specific fuel type consumed by the dispatched generating unit. Used for fuel cost allocation, emissions reporting, and EPA compliance. 'none' for non-fuel resources such as wind, solar, or demand response. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: natural_gas|coal|oil|uranium|water|wind|solar|none — promote to reference product]
reference: EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; EPA Clean Air Act; FERC Order 888

description: The heat rate of the generating unit at the dispatched MW setpoint, expressed in British Thermal Units per kilowatt-hour (BTU/kWh). Used for fuel consumption estimation, emissions calculations, and economic dispatch optimization.
reference: EIA Form 923; EPA eGRID; FERC Order 888; EPA Clean Air Act

description: Externally-known, human-readable business identifier for the dispatch instruction, used in operator logs, audit trails, and regulatory filings. Format: EMS-DISP-YYYY-NNNNNN.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; NERC EOP-001

description: Current lifecycle status of the dispatch instruction. Tracks the workflow from issuance through acknowledgment, execution, and completion or cancellation. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: issued|acknowledged|executing|completed|cancelled|rejected — promote to reference product if additional statuses are needed]
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC EOP-001; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: The precise date and time (with timezone offset) at which the EMS issued this dispatch instruction to the generating unit or controllable resource. This is the principal business event timestamp.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; NERC EOP-001

description: The Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in dollars per MWh at the dispatch node at the time this instruction was issued. Used for economic dispatch evaluation and post-dispatch settlement.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO LMP methodology

description: Reference to the pricing node at which the Locational Marginal Price (LMP) applies for this dispatch instruction. Used for economic dispatch optimization and settlement calculations.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO LMP methodology

description: Reference to the energy market interval (Day-Ahead Market or Real-Time Market) associated with this dispatch instruction. Links to the market scheduling system or ETRM (Allegro) interval record.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO tariff; LMP market rules

description: The energy market context under which this dispatch instruction is issued. DAM (Day-Ahead Market), RTM (Real-Time Market), bilateral contract, self-schedule, or none for purely reliability-driven dispatches.
reference: FERC Order 888; FERC Order 719; RTO/ISO tariff; LMP market rules

description: The target reactive power output level in Megavars (MVAR) instructed for voltage support purposes. Applicable when dispatch_reason is voltage_support or when reactive dispatch is co-optimized.
reference: NERC VAR-001; NERC VAR-002; FERC Order 888

description: The actual MW output achieved by the generating unit in response to this dispatch instruction, as measured by SCADA telemetry from OSIsoft PI Historian. Used to assess dispatch compliance and unit performance.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; OSIsoft PI Historian; EIA Form 923

description: The difference in MW between the instructed setpoint and the actual response (mw_actual_response minus mw_setpoint). Positive values indicate over-generation; negative values indicate under-generation. Used for NERC compliance analysis.

The change in MW output instructed by this dispatch (mw_setpoint minus mw_setpoint_prior). Positive values indicate an increase in generation; negative values indicate a decrease. Used for ramp compliance analysis.
The target real power output level in Megawatts (MW) that the generating unit or controllable resource is instructed to achieve. This is the principal quantitative dispatch directive.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1547; EIA Form 923

description: The MW setpoint that was in effect immediately before this dispatch instruction was issued. Used to calculate the MW delta and assess ramp requirements.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; OSIsoft PI Historian

description: Free-text notes entered by the EMS operator at the time of dispatch. May include context for manual overrides, reliability concerns, or coordination with other control areas.

The OSIsoft PI Historian tag name for the real-time MW output data stream of the dispatched generating unit. Enables direct linkage between dispatch instructions and PI Historian time-series data for operational analytics.
reference: OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82

description: The instructed rate of change in MW output, expressed in Megawatts per minute (MW/min), at which the generating unit should ramp to the new setpoint. Derived from unit capability and AGC parameters.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 888; IEEE Std 1547

description: Direction of frequency regulation service associated with this dispatch instruction. 'up' indicates regulation up (increase output); 'down' indicates regulation down (decrease output); 'none' for non-regulation dispatches.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NERC BAL-002; FERC Order 755

description: Free-text or coded reason provided by the resource operator when a dispatch instruction is rejected or not acknowledged. Used for reliability event analysis and operator performance review.

Type of operating reserve being activated by this dispatch instruction, if applicable. Spinning reserves are online and synchronized; non-spinning reserves can be brought online within 10 minutes; supplemental reserves provide longer-term backup.
reference: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; FERC Order 888; RTO/ISO tariff

description: The date and time at which the generating unit reached or was confirmed to be at the instructed MW setpoint, as recorded by SCADA telemetry.
reference: NERC BAL-001; OSIsoft PI Historian; GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: The originating operational system that generated this dispatch instruction. EMS for Energy Management System automated dispatch; AGC for Automatic Generation Control; DMS for Distribution Management System; OMS for Outage Management System; DERMS for Distributed Energy Resource Management System; manual for operator-entered instructions.
reference: GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS; OSIsoft PI Historian; NERC CIP-007

description: The date and time at which this dispatch instruction record was last modified in the Silver Layer data product. Used for incremental data processing and audit trail.
reference: NERC CIP-007; NIST SP 800-82; FASB ASC 980

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each energy balance record in the balancing area. Primary key for the energy_balance data product.
Foreign key linking to der.aggregation_group. Business justification: Energy balance reports are broken out by aggregation groups for market settlement and DER performance analysis.
Reference to the NERC-registered Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this energy balance record applies. Links to the balancing_area master record.

Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.
reference: NERC CIP-007, NERC BAL-001 operator accountability

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Energy Balance records are posted to the General Ledger for financial statements and regulatory filings.

Identifier of the system operator or EMS user responsible for reviewing or manually adjusting this energy balance record. Populated for manual entries or operator-confirmed revisions. Links to workforce/operator master data.
reference: NERC CIP-007, NERC BAL-001 operator accountability

description: Foreign key linking to product.rate_schedule. Business justification: Settlement report requires applying the correct rate schedule to each balancing area energy balance for billing compliance.
Foreign key linking to regulatory.rate_case. Business justification: Energy balance statements are submitted as part of rate‑case settlements; linking provides traceability to the specific rate case.

Average Area Control Error (ACE) over the interval period in Megawatts (MW). Used for NERC Control Performance Standard (CPS1/CPS2) compliance calculations and regulatory reporting to NERC and state PUCs.

Area Control Error (ACE) for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). ACE = (Actual Net Interchange – Scheduled Net Interchange) – 10B(Actual Frequency – Scheduled Frequency). Key NERC BAL-001 compliance metric measuring real-time generation-load balance.

Actual metered energy interchange across balancing area tie-lines during the interval, expressed in MWh. Compared against scheduled_interchange_mwh to compute interchange deviation for NERC BAL compliance.

NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score for the interval, expressed as a percentage. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE relative to frequency deviation. NERC requires a minimum 100% CPS1 score on a rolling 12-month basis.

Indicates whether the balancing area exceeded the NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) ACE limit (L10) during this interval. True = CPS2 violation occurred; False = within limits. Triggers mandatory NERC reporting when True.
Timestamp when this energy balance record was first created in the Silver Layer lakehouse, typically upon ingestion from SCADA/PI Historian or EMS. Audit trail field for data lineage.
reference: NERC BAL-001 data retention, FERC Order 890

description: Quality indicator for the energy balance record derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry quality flags. 'good' = validated telemetry; 'suspect' = questionable reading requiring review; 'estimated' = gap-filled or interpolated; 'bad' = failed quality check; 'missing' = no telemetry received.
reference: OSIsoft PI quality codes, NERC BAL-001 data quality requirements

description: Identifies the primary source system from which this energy balance record was derived. 'scada' = GE PowerOn SCADA telemetry; 'pi_historian' = OSIsoft PI Historian; 'ems' = Energy Management System calculated; 'manual' = operator-entered; 'estimated' = gap-filled estimate.

Net energy injected into the grid from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, battery storage, and small-scale generation during the interval, expressed in MWh. Tracked via DERMS integration.
reference: FERC Order 2222, NERC BAL-001, State NEM tariffs

description: Energy reduction achieved through Demand Response (DR) dispatch during the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents load curtailment from DR programs activated by the EMS/DERMS. Used for DR settlement and NERC BAL compliance.
reference: FERC Order 745, NERC BAL-002, FERC Order 2222

description: Indicates whether this energy balance record has been included in an EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. True = reported to EIA; False = pending submission. Supports regulatory reporting completeness tracking.

business_glossary_term: Energy Information Administration (EIA) Balancing Authority Code
description: EIA-assigned balancing authority code for the reporting entity. Required for EIA Form 930 (Hourly Electric Grid Monitor) submission. Uniquely identifies the balancing authority in EIA's national energy data system.
Timestamp when this energy balance record was promoted from 'preliminary' to 'final' status following validation. Marks the completion of the operational accounting close for the interval.

Total energy generated from fossil fuel sources (natural gas, coal, oil) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Used for emissions reporting to EPA and EIA.
reference: EIA Form 923, EPA Clean Air Act reporting, FERC Form 1

description: The frequency bias setting (B) applied in the ACE calculation formula for this interval, expressed in MW/Hz. Represents the balancing area's contribution to primary frequency response. Filed annually with NERC.

Average system frequency measured in Hertz (Hz) during the interval. Nominal value is 60.000 Hz for the North American interconnection. Deviations from nominal drive ACE calculations and frequency regulation dispatch.
reference: NERC BAL-003, NERC BAL-004, NERC FAC-001

description: Accumulated inadvertent energy interchange for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the difference between actual and scheduled interchange that must be repaid to neighboring balancing areas per NERC BAL-005 payback requirements.
North American electrical interconnection to which this balancing area belongs. Determines synchronous frequency reference and reliability coordinator jurisdiction.
Duration of the energy balance interval in minutes (e.g., 5, 15, 30, 60). Distinguishes sub-hourly from hourly records and supports aggregation logic.
The ending timestamp of the energy accounting interval. Together with interval_start_timestamp defines the precise measurement window for this balance record.

The beginning timestamp of the energy accounting interval (hourly or sub-hourly) for which this balance record is computed. Derived from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry. Conforms to ISO 8601 format yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX.
reference: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, EIA Form 930

description: Difference between actual total load and forecasted load for the interval, expressed in MWh (actual minus forecast). Positive value indicates load exceeded forecast; negative indicates load was below forecast. Used to evaluate forecasting accuracy and improve EMS models.

Forecasted energy load for the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Generated by the EMS load forecasting module prior to the operating interval. Used to compute forecast error and support dispatch planning.
reference: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, EIA Form 930

description: Indicates whether this energy balance interval is fully compliant with applicable NERC BAL reliability standards (BAL-001, BAL-002, BAL-003, BAL-005). True = compliant; False = one or more NERC BAL standard violations detected. Triggers compliance workflow when False.
reference: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-002, NERC BAL-003, NERC BAL-005

description: NERC e-Tag identifier associated with the scheduled interchange transactions contributing to this energy balance interval. Used for cross-referencing with NERC e-Tag system for interchange scheduling and curtailment tracking.

Net energy exchanged across the balancing area boundary during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Positive value indicates net export; negative value indicates net import. Computed as sum of all scheduled and actual tie-line flows.
reference: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-005, FERC Order 890

description: Total energy generated from nuclear sources within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Reported separately per NRC and EIA requirements.
The calendar date (in local prevailing time) to which this energy balance interval belongs. Used for daily aggregation, settlement, and regulatory reporting aligned to the operating day.
reference: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 930, FERC Order 890

description: The hour of the operating day (0–23) in which this interval falls, expressed in local prevailing time. Used for hourly aggregation, TOU analysis, and RTO/ISO settlement hour alignment.
Total operating reserve available in the balancing area at the start of the interval, expressed in Megawatts (MW). Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.
reference: NERC BAL-002, NERC BAL-003, RTO/ISO reserve requirements

description: Lifecycle status of the energy balance record indicating its processing and settlement state. 'preliminary' = near-real-time estimate; 'final' = validated operational accounting; 'revised' = corrected after initial finalization; 'settled' = accepted by RTO/ISO for financial settlement; 'void' = invalidated record.
reference: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890, RTO/ISO settlement protocols

description: Total energy generated from renewable sources (wind, solar, hydro, geothermal, biomass) within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Subset of total_generation_mwh. Supports Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking and IRP reporting.
reference: EIA Form 923, FERC Form 1, State RPS requirements

description: Sequential revision counter for this energy balance record. Starts at 0 for the initial preliminary record and increments with each correction or resettlement. Supports audit trail and version management for regulatory submissions.
reference: NERC BAL-001, FERC Order 890 data retention requirements

description: Free-text description of the reason for the most recent revision to this energy balance record (e.g., 'meter data correction', 'SCADA telemetry gap fill', 'RTO settlement adjustment'). Populated only when revision_number > 0.

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization / Independent System Operator (RTO/ISO) Code
description: Code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) with which this balancing area is affiliated for market settlement and reliability coordination (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, SPP, ERCOT, NYISO, ISO-NE).
reference: FERC Order 888, FERC Order 2000, NERC registration

description: Total energy interchange scheduled across balancing area tie-lines for the interval, expressed in MWh. Represents the Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or intra-day scheduled position prior to real-time deviations.
reference: NERC BAL-001, NERC BAL-005, FERC Order 890

description: Timestamp when this energy balance record was accepted and confirmed by the RTO/ISO for financial settlement. Marks the completion of the market settlement lifecycle for the interval.

Identifies the market settlement period type for this energy balance record. 'real_time' = RTM interval data; 'day_ahead' = DAM scheduled position; 'final_settlement' = post-operating-day settlement; 'resettlement' = corrected settlement after dispute resolution.
reference: FERC Order 890, RTO/ISO tariff settlement protocols

description: Spinning (synchronized) reserve available in the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MW. Subset of operating_reserve_mw representing generation online and capable of immediate response. NERC BAL-002 compliance metric.

Total electrical energy generated within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Aggregates all generation resources including fossil fuel, nuclear, and renewable sources. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.
reference: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 923, FERC Form 1

description: Total electrical energy consumed by load within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in Megawatt-Hours (MWh). Represents native load plus losses. Sourced from SCADA/PI Historian telemetry.
reference: NERC BAL-001, EIA Form 930, FERC Order 890

description: Estimated electrical energy lost in transmission and distribution within the balancing area during the interval, expressed in MWh. Used in energy accounting identity: Generation = Load + Net Interchange + Losses.
reference: NERC BAL-001, FERC Form 1, EIA Form 930

description: Timestamp of the most recent update to this energy balance record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Updated on each revision, status change, or data quality correction.
reference: NERC BAL-001 data retention, FERC Order 890

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each load forecast record in the balancing area Energy Management System (EMS) forecasting engine. Primary key for the load_forecast data product.

Reference to the NERC-defined Balancing Authority Area (BAA) for which this load forecast was produced. The balancing area is the fundamental geographic and operational unit for which the EMS maintains load-generation balance. Links to the balancing area master reference product.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: Reference to the specific control zone or load zone within the balancing area for which this forecast applies. Control zones represent sub-areas of the transmission system with distinct load characteristics, used for Locational Marginal Price (LMP) and zonal load forecasting.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

description: Foreign key linking to gridops.weather_forecast. Business justification: Load forecasts are derived from a specific weather forecast; FK links forecast source.

The observed actual electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the forecast interval, populated post-interval from SCADA telemetry or OSIsoft PI Historian. Null until the interval has elapsed and actuals are available. Used for forecast accuracy tracking and model performance evaluation.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; OSIsoft PI Historian

description: The lower bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the minimum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for probabilistic unit commitment and reserve margin planning.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

description: The upper bound of the statistical confidence interval for the forecasted demand in Megawatts (MW). Represents the maximum plausible demand at the specified confidence level. Used for contingency planning and operating reserve determination.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

description: The statistical confidence level expressed as a percentage (e.g., 90.00, 95.00) associated with the confidence interval bounds. Indicates the probability that actual demand will fall within the stated confidence interval bounds.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

description: The number of Cooling Degree Days (CDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature exceeds 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify cooling-driven electrical demand.
reference: EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards; IRP regulatory filings

description: Audit timestamp recording when this load forecast record was first persisted into the Silver Layer lakehouse. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and SLA compliance tracking. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
reference: NERC CIP-008; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FASB ASC 980

description: Classification of the forecast day by its load profile category. Weekday, weekend, and holiday designations drive distinct load shape patterns in the EMS forecasting model. Peak day and off-peak day classifications support Time-of-Use (TOU) and Critical Peak Pricing (CPP) rate analysis.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; TOU/CPP rate tariff definitions

description: The forecasted generation output in Megawatts (MW) from Distributed Energy Resources (DER) including rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage, and small-scale generation within the distribution system. Subtracted from gross load to derive net load. Sourced from DERMS forecasting.
reference: FERC Order 2222; NERC BAL-001; DERMS operational standards

description: The amount of Demand Response (DR) capacity in Megawatts (MW) that has been dispatched or is planned to be dispatched during this forecast interval. Represents load reduction committed through DR programs, reducing the net load the grid must serve. Used for DR dispatch planning and DERMS coordination.
reference: FERC Order 745; NERC BAL-001; DERMS operational standards

description: The calendar date for which the load forecast applies. For day-ahead forecasts this is the operating day being forecasted. Used for daily operations planning, Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling, and next-day unit commitment.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: The absolute difference between forecasted demand and actual demand in Megawatts (MW), calculated as actual_demand_mw minus forecasted_demand_mw. Positive values indicate under-forecasting; negative values indicate over-forecasting. Populated post-interval for accuracy tracking.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; EIA Form 930

description: The forecast error expressed as a percentage of actual demand, calculated as (actual_demand_mw - forecasted_demand_mw) / actual_demand_mw * 100. Used as the primary KPI for EMS forecasting model accuracy assessment and NERC compliance reporting.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031

description: Classification of the forecast by its planning horizon. Short-term covers hourly/daily intervals; medium-term covers weekly/monthly; persistence uses the last observed value as the forecast; day-ahead supports Day-Ahead Market (DAM) scheduling; real-time supports Real-Time Market (RTM) dispatch. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: short_term|medium_term|long_term|persistence|day_ahead|real_time — promote to reference product]
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: The forecasted relative humidity percentage used as a secondary weather input to the load forecasting model. Humidity affects the heat index and cooling load, particularly for residential and commercial air conditioning demand.
reference: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

description: The ending date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. Together with forecast_interval_start, defines the precise time window of the forecast. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: The beginning date and time of the interval for which the load demand is being forecasted. For hourly forecasts this marks the top of the hour; for daily forecasts this marks midnight. Used for unit commitment scheduling, interchange scheduling, and DR dispatch planning. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: The name or identifier of the load forecasting algorithm or model used to produce this forecast (e.g., regression-based, neural network, ensemble). Supports model governance, audit trail, and comparison of forecast accuracy across different modeling approaches in the EMS.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

description: The version string of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast (e.g., '3.2.1'). Enables traceability of forecast outputs to specific model releases, supporting model validation, regulatory audit, and accuracy benchmarking.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

description: Reference to the specific version of the EMS load forecasting model used to produce this forecast. Enables accuracy tracking across model versions, supports model governance, and facilitates comparison of forecast performance between model iterations.
reference: NERC BAL-001; NIST Smart Grid Framework; FERC Order 764

description: Free-text field for operational notes, qualitative adjustments, or override justifications applied to this forecast record by EMS operators. Captures manual interventions, special event adjustments (e.g., major sporting events, industrial shutdowns), or model override rationale for audit and review purposes.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; internal EMS operational procedures

description: Externally-known business identifier assigned by the EMS forecasting engine to uniquely identify a specific forecast run or batch. Used to group all interval records produced in a single forecast execution cycle. Aligns with OSIsoft PI Historian and GE PowerOn EMS run identifiers.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930

description: The date and time at which the EMS forecasting engine initiated and completed the forecast run that produced this record. This is the principal business event timestamp representing when the forecast was generated, distinct from the interval being forecasted. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; OSIsoft PI Historian

description: Current lifecycle state of the forecast record. Draft indicates the forecast is being generated; published indicates it has been released for operational use; superseded indicates a newer forecast run has replaced it; archived indicates it has been retained for historical accuracy tracking; cancelled indicates the run was aborted.

The forecasted ambient temperature in degrees Fahrenheit used as the primary weather input to the load forecasting model for this interval. Temperature is the dominant weather driver of electrical load in most utility service territories.
reference: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

description: The primary forecasted electrical load demand in Megawatts (MW) for the specified interval. This is the principal quantitative output of the EMS forecasting engine, used for unit commitment, interchange scheduling, and next-day operations planning.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; NERC MOD-031

description: The number of Heating Degree Days (HDD) for the forecast date, calculated as the number of degrees the mean daily temperature falls below 65°F. A standard weather normalization metric used in load forecasting models to quantify heating-driven electrical and gas demand.
reference: EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards; IRP regulatory filings

description: The scheduled net interchange in Megawatts (MW) with neighboring balancing areas or the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO)/Independent System Operator (ISO) for this forecast interval. Positive values indicate net imports; negative values indicate net exports. Used in balancing area control and unit commitment.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC INT-006

description: The length of the forecast interval in minutes (e.g., 15, 30, 60, 1440 for daily). Determines the granularity of the forecast and aligns with Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) interval data and SCADA telemetry resolution.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; AMI standards

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval falls within a designated peak demand period as defined by the utility's tariff or operational planning criteria. Used to identify intervals requiring heightened operational attention, DR dispatch readiness, and capacity reserve verification.
reference: NERC BAL-001; PUC tariff definitions; TOU/CPP rate structures

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast interval is associated with a declared reliability event (e.g., emergency operating condition, NERC alert, extreme weather advisory). When true, the forecast may have been produced under emergency protocols with modified model parameters.
reference: NERC EOP-011; NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764

description: Boolean flag indicating whether an EMS operator manually overrode the model-generated forecast value for this interval. When true, the forecasted_demand_mw reflects an operator-adjusted value rather than the raw model output. Supports audit trail and model accuracy analysis.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; internal EMS operational procedures

description: The forecasted net load in Megawatts (MW) after subtracting Distributed Energy Resources (DER) generation (e.g., rooftop solar, behind-the-meter storage) from gross forecasted demand. Net load is the actual generation requirement that dispatchable resources must meet. Critical for unit commitment and interchange scheduling.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; DERMS operational standards; EIA Form 930

description: The NERC-defined operating day (midnight to midnight local time) to which this forecast record belongs. Distinct from forecast_date in that it represents the grid operations scheduling day used by the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) for market and reliability purposes.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

description: The minimum operating reserve requirement in Megawatts (MW) for this forecast interval, derived from the forecasted load and NERC reliability standards. Includes spinning and non-spinning reserves required to maintain grid reliability. Used for unit commitment and capacity planning.
reference: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-003; FERC Order 764

description: The estimated peak electrical demand in Megawatts (MW) expected within the forecast period. Critical for capacity planning, reserve margin calculations, and Demand Response (DR) dispatch planning. Used in General Rate Case (GRC) filings and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) submissions.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; PUC rate case filings

description: Boolean flag indicating whether this forecast record is designated for inclusion in regulatory reporting submissions (e.g., EIA Form 930, FERC filings, NERC reliability assessments, PUC rate case filings). Supports automated extraction of reportable forecast data for compliance workflows.
reference: EIA Form 930; FERC Order 764; NERC MOD-031; PUC reporting requirements

business_glossary_term: Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) / Independent System Operator (ISO) Code
description: The code identifying the Regional Transmission Organization (RTO) or Independent System Operator (ISO) market in which this balancing area participates (e.g., PJM, MISO, CAISO, ERCOT, SPP). Determines the market rules, scheduling protocols, and reporting requirements applicable to this forecast.
reference: FERC Order 2000; FERC Order 764; RTO/ISO tariff definitions

description: The utility-defined operating season for the forecast interval. Seasonal classification drives load shape selection in the EMS forecasting model and aligns with seasonal rate structures, capacity planning periods, and NERC reliability assessments.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; PUC seasonal rate filings

description: Code identifying the operational system of record that produced or supplied this load forecast record. Supports data lineage and provenance tracking in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Values correspond to the utility's operational systems including the Energy Management System (EMS), SCADA, OSIsoft PI Historian, Distribution Management System (DMS), Outage Management System (OMS), and DERMS. reference: NIST Smart Grid Framework; NERC CIP-008; FERC Order 764

description: Audit timestamp recording the most recent modification to this load forecast record, such as when actual demand values were populated post-interval or when the forecast status was updated. Stored in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX).
reference: NERC CIP-008; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: The weather-normalized baseline load demand in Megawatts (MW), representing what demand would be under normal or reference weather conditions. Used to isolate weather-driven load variability from underlying demand trends for regulatory reporting and Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) analysis.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC Order 764; EIA Form 930; IRP regulatory filings

description: Reference to the primary weather station or weather data source used to supply temperature, humidity, and other meteorological inputs to the load forecasting model for this forecast interval. Weather normalization is a core component of EMS load forecasting.
reference: NERC BAL-001; EIA Form 930; NOAA weather data standards

reference: NERC CIP-007-6, OSIsoft PI Historian, GE PowerOn Advanced DMS/OMS

description: Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.
Reference to the grid control zone or balancing area associated with this log entry. Links to the gridops.control_zone master record for geographic and operational context.

Reference to the licensed control room operator who authored this log entry. Links to the workforce/employee master record. Required for NERC CIP personnel accountability and shift responsibility tracking.

Reference to the primary grid asset (substation, transformer, feeder, generator, transmission line, etc.) associated with this log entry. Links to the asset management master record in Maximo EAM. Null if the entry is not asset-specific.

business_glossary_term: SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) Point ID
description: The SCADA data point or tag identifier from OSIsoft PI Historian associated with the measurement or control action referenced in this log entry. Enables direct linkage to real-time operational data for post-event analysis.
Reference to the operational shift during which this log entry was created. Enables shift-level aggregation of events, handover documentation, and accountability reporting.

Reference to the shift supervisor who reviewed or approved this log entry. Required for entries of critical or high priority. Supports supervisory accountability and NERC CIP-004 personnel management compliance.

The Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) recorded at the time of the log entry. ACE is the real-time difference between actual and scheduled interchange, adjusted for frequency deviation. Critical metric for balancing area control and NERC BAL-001 compliance.
Ambient air temperature in degrees Celsius recorded at the time of the log entry. Relevant for thermal loading analysis, equipment derating, and weather-related event context.
The date and time when this log entry was formally approved as part of the official operational record. Null if not yet approved. Required for regulatory audit trail integrity.

Human-readable asset identifier or tag number (e.g., substation name, feeder ID, equipment tag) as recorded by the operator at time of entry. Preserved as entered to maintain the original operational record even if the asset master record changes.

File path, document management system reference, or URL pointing to supporting documentation attached to this log entry (e.g., switching order PDF, alarm printout, event report). Null if no attachment.

NERC Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) impact classification of the asset or action referenced in this log entry. Determines the level of cybersecurity and physical security controls applicable. Required for NERC CIP-002 asset categorization compliance.
The method or channel used for the communication recorded in this log entry. Relevant for NERC COM-001 compliance which mandates reliable communication facilities for grid operators.

The name or identifier of the external or internal party involved in a communication log entry (e.g., RTO/ISO operator name, neighboring utility, field crew ID, supervisor name). Populated for communication entry types.

The measured system frequency in Hertz (Hz) at the time of the log entry, as recorded by the operator or captured from SCADA. Relevant for frequency regulation events and under-frequency load shedding actions. Nominal value is 60.0000 Hz for North American grids.
The measured or dispatched generation output in Megawatts (MW) referenced in this log entry. Relevant for generation dispatch, curtailment, and unit commitment actions.

The measured or observed load in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the log entry. Relevant for load shedding, demand response dispatch, and load balancing actions. Null if not applicable to the entry type.

Externally-known, human-readable sequential identifier for the log entry (e.g., OL-2024-00123456). Used for cross-referencing in regulatory audits, NERC compliance filings, and post-event analysis reports.

Free-text narrative entered by the operator describing the action taken, observation made, alarm acknowledged, or communication recorded. Business classification of the alarm condition: thermal_overload (conductor or transformer heating), voltage_violation (over/under voltage), frequency_deviation (grid frequency out of range), equipment_failure (device malfunction), communication_loss (telemetry failure), or protection_system (relay or breaker operation).

The ACE threshold in Megawatts (MW) that, when exceeded, triggers a compliance event or corrective action. Derived from the Balancing Authority's frequency bias setting and NERC BAL-001 control performance standards.

Instantaneous Area Control Error (ACE) value in Megawatts (MW) at the time of the event. ACE represents the difference between actual and scheduled net interchange, adjusted for frequency bias. This is the authoritative ACE measurement for NERC BAL-001 real power balancing compliance.

business_glossary_term: Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) Exceedance Flag
description: Indicates whether the Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) was exceeded during this event. True if ACE exceeded the BAAL threshold as defined in NERC BAL-001-2, triggering mandatory corrective action and potential compliance reporting.

The upper Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary.

The lower Balancing Authority ACE Limit (BAAL) threshold in Megawatts (MW) applicable during this event interval. Defined per NERC BAL-001-2 and used to assess whether the balancing authority exceeded its allowable ACE boundary on the under-generation side.

NERC-assigned alphanumeric code identifying the Balancing Authority control area where the event occurred. Used in NERC compliance filings, RTO/ISO interchange scheduling, and energy balance reporting.
reference: NERC BAL-001; FERC; NERC Reliability Standards

description: Narrative description of the corrective actions taken by the EMS/AGC system or grid operators to restore frequency and ACE to within compliance limits. Includes AGC dispatch instructions, manual operator interventions, and emergency procedures. Required for NERC BAL-002 disturbance control documentation.
reference: NERC BAL-002; NERC BAL-001; GE PowerOn EMS

description: NERC Control Performance Standard 1 (CPS1) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS1 measures the one-minute average ACE divided by the frequency error, with a minimum compliance threshold of 100%. Values below 100% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.

NERC Control Performance Standard 2 (CPS2) compliance score as a percentage for the reporting interval. CPS2 measures the 10-minute average ACE against the L10 limit, with a minimum compliance threshold of 90%. Values below 90% indicate non-compliance with NERC BAL-001.
The date and time (UTC) when this frequency regulation event record was first created in the data lakehouse Silver layer. Used for data lineage, audit trail, and ETL reconciliation.

description: Operational severity classification of the frequency regulation event based on the magnitude of frequency deviation, ACE exceedance, and system impact. Used for prioritizing operator response, escalation workflows, and post-event reliability analysis.

Magnitude of frequency deviation from the 60 Hz nominal in Hertz (Hz). Positive values indicate over-frequency; negative values indicate under-frequency. Key metric for NERC BAL-003 frequency response obligation compliance and disturbance analysis.

description: The date the technician began active field service in their current craft or role. May differ from hire_date if the technician transferred from a non-field role or changed craft classification. Used for craft seniority calculations and CBA compliance.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0000; Collective Bargaining Agreement

description: The geographic service territory or district to which the technician is primarily assigned for T&D operations, O&M dispatch, and emergency response. Aligns with GIS-defined service territory boundaries in Esri ArcGIS. Sourced from ClickSoftware WFM.
reference: ClickSoftware WFM; Esri ArcGIS; GE PowerOn DMS/OMS

description: The emergency storm response mobilization tier assigned to the technician, defining their priority and role during major outage events. Tier 1 = immediate first responders; Tier 2 = secondary wave; Tier 3 = support/logistics; Exempt = not required for storm duty. Used by OMS and ClickSoftware WFM for emergency staffing.
reference: ClickSoftware WFM; GE PowerOn OMS; NERC CIP; Collective Bargaining Agreement

description: The SAP personnel number of the technician's direct supervisor or crew foreman. Used for approval workflows, OSHA incident reporting chain of command, and dispatch escalation. Sourced from SAP HR Infotype 0001 (Organizational Assignment).

The date the technician's employment was terminated, if applicable. Null for active employees. Used to deactivate dispatch eligibility, revoke system access, and support workforce attrition reporting. Sourced from SAP HR Infotype 0000.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0000; OSHA 29 CFR 1910; FASB ASC 980

description: The maximum travel radius in miles from the technician's base location that they are contractually or operationally authorized to travel for work assignments under normal (non-storm) conditions. Used by ClickSoftware WFM for geographic dispatch optimization.

The labor union to which the technician belongs, if any. Drives application of collective bargaining agreement (CBA) rules for scheduling, overtime, dispatch priority, and grievance management. Common affiliations include IBEW (International Brotherhood of Electrical Workers) and UWUA (Utility Workers Union of America). Sourced from SAP HR Infotype 0011.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0011; National Labor Relations Act (NLRA); Collective Bargaining Agreement

description: The specific local chapter number of the union to which the technician belongs (e.g., IBEW Local 1245). Required for CBA compliance, grievance tracking, and labor reporting. Null for non-union and management employees. Sourced from SAP HR.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0011; National Labor Relations Act (NLRA); Collective Bargaining Agreement

description: The fleet asset code of the utility vehicle (bucket truck, service van, digger derrick, etc.) currently assigned to the technician for field operations. Used for fleet management, GPS tracking integration, and work order costing. Sourced from Maximo EAM or fleet management system.

description: The SAP HR work schedule rule code defining the technician's standard shift pattern (e.g., 4x10, 5x8, rotating shift, on-call). Drives ClickSoftware WFM availability windows, overtime eligibility, and CBA compliance for scheduling. Sourced from SAP HR Infotype 0007.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0007; ClickSoftware WFM; Collective Bargaining Agreement

description: The hierarchical skill and responsibility classification of the technician within their craft. Determines pay grade, work assignment eligibility, and supervisory authority on crew dispatches. Sourced from SAP HR Infotype 0001 and union agreement tables.
reference: SAP HR Infotype 0001; OSHA 29 CFR 1910.269; Collective Bargaining Agreement

Unique identifier for the work order assignment record. Primary key for this transactional dispatch entity linking workforce resources to work execution tasks.
Reference to the crew or team assigned to this work order when the assignment is for a multi-person crew rather than an individual technician. Nullable when assignment is to a single technician.

Reference to the individual technician, lineworker, meter reader, or field service personnel assigned to this work order. Links to the workforce employee master record in SAP HR or ClickSoftware resource pool.
reference: SAP HR Personnel Number, ClickSoftware Resource ID

description: Reference to the parent work order from Maximo EAM or GE PowerOn OMS that this assignment fulfills. Links the dispatch record to the underlying maintenance, construction, or service task.
reference: Maximo Work Order Object, GE PowerOn Work Order

description: Actual date and time when the technician or crew arrived at the work site, typically captured via mobile device GPS or manual check-in. Used for SLA compliance tracking and labor costing.
Actual date and time when the technician or crew departed the work site, typically captured via mobile device. Used for travel time calculation and next-assignment routing.
Actual date and time when work was completed on site. Used for labor costing, productivity metrics, and work order closure processing.
reference: ClickSoftware Actual End, Maximo Actual Finish

description: Actual date and time when work began on site, distinct from arrival time. Captures the moment active work commenced, used for labor tracking and productivity analysis.
reference: ClickSoftware Actual Start, Maximo Actual Start

description: Free-text notes or special instructions for the technician or crew regarding this assignment. May include site access instructions, customer contact information, safety warnings, or work-specific guidance.
reference: ClickSoftware Assignment Notes, Maximo Long Description

description: Human-readable business identifier for this assignment, typically generated by ClickSoftware WFM or the dispatching system. Used for operational tracking and communication with field personnel.

Current lifecycle state of the work order assignment. Tracks the progression from initial dispatch through field execution to completion or cancellation. Updated by mobile workforce application or dispatcher. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: dispatched|en_route|on_site|in_progress|completed|cancelled|suspended|reassigned — 8 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Classification of the assignment based on the nature and urgency of the work. Distinguishes between planned maintenance, emergency response, storm restoration, and other operational categories.
reference: ClickSoftware Assignment Type, Maximo Work Type

description: Code identifying the reason for assignment cancellation when status is cancelled. Used for operational analysis and process improvement. Nullable when assignment is not cancelled. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: customer_cancelled|weather|equipment_unavailable|crew_unavailable|duplicate|work_completed_by_other — promote to reference product]

Indicates whether specific certifications or qualifications are required for this assignment (e.g., OSHA safety training, CDL, confined space entry). True when certifications are mandatory, False otherwise.
Date and time when this assignment record was first created in the source system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.

Indicates whether this assignment requires a scheduled customer appointment or access to customer premises. True when customer coordination is required, False for utility-side work. Used for appointment window tracking and customer communication.
Date and time when the assignment was dispatched to the technician or crew by the workforce management system or dispatcher. Represents the official start of the assignment lifecycle.

Indicates whether specialized equipment or vehicles are required for this assignment (e.g., bucket truck, digger derrick, cable splicer). True when special equipment is needed, False for standard assignments.
Date and time when this assignment record was last updated in the source system. Used for change tracking and data synchronization.

Indicates whether the technician acknowledged receipt of the assignment via mobile device. True when acknowledged, False when not yet acknowledged. Used for dispatch confirmation and communication tracking.
Date and time when the technician acknowledged the assignment via mobile device. Used for response time tracking and dispatcher confirmation.
Total time in minutes spent on site from arrival to departure. Calculated as the difference between actual departure and actual arrival timestamps. Used for labor costing and productivity metrics.

Indicates whether this assignment is related to a customer outage or service interruption. True for outage restoration work, False for non-outage work. Used for reliability metrics (SAIDI, SAIFI, CAIDI) and priority dispatch.

Indicates whether this assignment is eligible for overtime compensation based on time of day, day of week, or assignment type. True when overtime rules apply, False for regular time. Used for labor costing and payroll integration.
reference: SAP HR Time Management, Union Agreement

description: Business priority level for this assignment, determining dispatch sequence and resource allocation. Critical assignments (e.g., public safety hazards, major outages) receive immediate attention.
Number of times this work order has been reassigned to different technicians or crews. Used for dispatch efficiency analysis and work order complexity assessment. Zero for first-time assignments.

Code identifying known safety hazards at the work site (e.g., energized equipment, confined space, traffic hazard, hazardous materials). Used for crew safety briefings and OSHA compliance. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: energized_equipment|confined_space|traffic_hazard|hazmat|fall_hazard|excavation|overhead_lines — promote to reference product]
Planned date and time when the work is expected to be completed. Used for scheduling optimization, customer communication, and capacity planning.
Planned date and time when the technician or crew is expected to begin work on site. Used for crew scheduling, customer appointment windows, and resource planning.
Geographic service territory or district where the work is being performed. Used for crew routing, jurisdiction tracking, and regional reporting. Aligns with utility service area boundaries.

Primary skill or qualification required for this assignment (e.g., lineworker, electrician, meter technician, gas fitter). Used for crew matching and certification compliance. Aligns with union job classifications.

Code identifying the operational system that originated this assignment record (ClickSoftware WFM, Maximo EAM, GE PowerOn OMS, SAP PM, or manual dispatch). Used for data lineage and system integration tracking.

Indicates whether this assignment is part of an emergency storm restoration effort. True for storm-related work, False for normal operations. Used for mutual aid tracking and regulatory reporting (SAIDI/SAIFI exclusions).
reference: GE PowerOn Storm Mode, NERC EOP

description: Total travel time in minutes from the technician's previous location to the work site. Used for labor costing, route optimization, and workforce productivity analysis.
Code identifying the applicable collective bargaining agreement or union contract governing this assignment. Used for labor costing, overtime rules, and crew assignment compliance.

Actual productive work time in minutes, calculated as the difference between actual start and actual end timestamps. Excludes setup, breaks, and non-productive time. Used for labor costing and efficiency analysis.
reference: Maximo Labor Hours, ClickSoftware Work Duration

description: Street address or location description of the work site. Used for crew navigation, customer communication, and operational reporting. May include customer premises or utility infrastructure locations.
reference: Oracle CC&B Service Address, GIS Location

description: Geographic latitude coordinate of the work site in decimal degrees. Used for mobile navigation, crew routing, and geospatial analysis. Sourced from GIS or mobile device GPS.
Geographic longitude coordinate of the work site in decimal degrees. Used for mobile navigation, crew routing, and geospatial analysis. Sourced from GIS or mobile device GPS.
