reference: IRS Publication 946 MACRS Property Classes; FASB ASC 740; Revenue Procedure 87-56

business_glossary_term: Maximo Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) Asset ID
description: Cross-reference identifier linking this financial fixed asset record to the corresponding physical asset record in Maximo Enterprise Asset Management (EAM). Enables reconciliation between financial accounting (SAP FI-AA) and physical asset management (Maximo) for O&M cost allocation and maintenance history.
reference: Maximo EAM Asset Master; ISO 55000 Asset Management; SAP-Maximo Integration

description: Current net book value of the asset computed as original cost minus accumulated depreciation (book basis). Represents the carrying amount on the balance sheet and is a key input to rate base (RAB) valuation. Expressed in USD.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-35; FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Case Cost-of-Service Studies

description: Original cost of the asset at the time of acquisition or construction completion, representing the gross plant investment recorded in the utility plant accounts. Basis for FERC Form 1 gross plant reporting, rate base (RAB) calculation, and depreciation base. Expressed in USD.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 360-10-30 Initial Measurement; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Utility Plant

description: Physical location or facility where the asset is installed or operated (e.g., 'Riverside Generating Station', 'Substation 47 - North District', 'Gas Compressor Station 12'). Used for geographic rate base allocation and GIS integration with Esri ArcGIS.
reference: SAP FI-AA Asset Location; Esri ArcGIS Geospatial Asset Registry; FERC Form 1

description: SAP MM purchase order number associated with the procurement of this asset. Provides traceability from the capitalized asset back to the original procurement transaction for audit and CAPEX tracking purposes.
reference: SAP MM Purchase Order; CAPEX Procurement Process; FASB ASC 360 Capitalization

description: Reason code explaining why the asset is excluded from the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) when rab_included is False. Used in rate case testimony and PUC filings to document plant disallowances or exclusions.
reference: State PUC Rate Case Orders; FASB ASC 980-360; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether this asset is included in the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) for rate case cost-of-service studies. Assets excluded from RAB (e.g., assets not used and useful, excess capacity, or disallowed plant) do not earn a return in rates. Critical for rate case preparation and PUC filings.
reference: State PUC Rate Case Orders; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; IRP Regulatory Asset Base Definition

description: Total depreciation accumulated using the PUC-approved regulatory depreciation rate from in-service date through current period. Differences between regulatory and book accumulated depreciation create regulatory assets or liabilities under FASB ASC 980. Expressed in USD.
reference: FASB ASC 980-360; State PUC Rate Case Orders; FERC Form 1

description: Depreciation method approved by the state PUC or FERC for regulatory ratemaking purposes. May differ from book depreciation method, creating regulatory assets or liabilities under FASB ASC 980. Used in rate case cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1 regulatory depreciation schedules.
reference: FASB ASC 980-360 Regulated Operations Plant; State PUC Depreciation Study Orders; FERC Form 1

description: Annual depreciation rate approved by the state PUC or FERC for ratemaking purposes, expressed as a decimal. May differ from book depreciation rate, creating regulatory timing differences. Filed in rate case depreciation studies and FERC Form 1.
reference: State PUC Depreciation Study Orders; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980-360

description: Estimated remaining service life of the asset in years as of the last depreciation study or reporting period. Used in remaining-life depreciation method calculations and impairment assessments. Key input for rate case depreciation expense projections.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-35 Remaining Life Method; State PUC Depreciation Studies; FERC Form 1

description: Estimated cost of removing or retiring the asset at end of useful life (cost of removal). For regulated utilities, net salvage (salvage value minus removal cost) is used in depreciation rate calculations filed with the PUC. Expressed in USD.
reference: FASB ASC 410-20 Asset Retirement Obligations; State PUC Depreciation Studies; FERC Form 1

description: Actual cost incurred to retire and remove the asset from service, including demolition, dismantling, and site remediation costs. Compared against the removal cost estimate for depreciation study accuracy assessment. Expressed in USD.
reference: FASB ASC 410-20 Asset Retirement Obligations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108.1; State PUC Depreciation Studies

description: Date the asset was retired or removed from service. Triggers cessation of depreciation and initiates retirement accounting entries including removal of original cost and accumulated depreciation from plant accounts. Null for active assets.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-40 Derecognition; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 108; SAP FI-AA Retirement

description: Classification of the asset retirement event. Normal retirements occur at end of useful life; abnormal retirements occur prematurely due to storm damage, obsolescence, or regulatory disallowance. Abandonment may trigger regulatory asset treatment under FASB ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-40; FASB ASC 980-360 Abandonment; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Orders

description: Estimated residual or salvage value of the asset at the end of its useful life, used to determine the depreciable base (original cost minus salvage value). Established through depreciation studies filed with state PUCs. Expressed in USD.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-35; State PUC Depreciation Study Requirements; FERC Form 1

description: Two-letter US state code identifying the regulatory jurisdiction under which this asset is rate-based. Determines which state PUC has authority over the asset's inclusion in rates. Critical for multi-state utilities performing jurisdictional cost allocation.
reference: State PUC Jurisdictional Allocation; FERC Form 1; NARUC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Total depreciation accumulated for federal income tax purposes (MACRS basis) from in-service date through current period. The difference between tax and book accumulated depreciation represents the temporary timing difference driving deferred income tax balances under FASB ASC 740 and ASC 980. Expressed in USD.
reference: IRS Publication 946; FASB ASC 740; FASB ASC 980-740; SAP FI-AA Depreciation Area 15

description: Depreciation method applied for federal income tax purposes. Most utility assets use Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS) per IRS guidelines, creating timing differences between book and tax depreciation that generate deferred income tax liabilities tracked under FASB ASC 980. Corresponds to SAP FI-AA depreciation area 15.
reference: IRS Publication 946 MACRS; FASB ASC 740 Income Taxes; FASB ASC 980-740 Regulated Operations Tax; SAP FI-AA Depreciation Area 15

description: Estimated useful service life of the asset in years as established by the PUC-approved depreciation study. Drives the straight-line depreciation rate. For group depreciation, this represents the average service life of the asset group. Corresponds to SAP FI-AA 'Useful Life' field.
reference: FASB ASC 360-10-35; State PUC Depreciation Study; SAP FI-AA Useful Life; FERC Form 1

description: SAP MM vendor number identifying the supplier from whom the asset was procured. Used for procurement analytics, vendor performance tracking, and supply chain cost analysis for capital projects.
reference: SAP MM Vendor Master; SAP FI-AA Asset Procurement; Supply Chain Management

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each rate base record in the regulatory asset base (RAB) calculation dataset. Primary key for the rate_base data product.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Foreign key linking to finance.regulatory_asset. Business justification: Rate Base calculations depend on regulatory asset data; linking provides direct access.

Total accumulated depreciation on utility plant in service as of the test year end date. Subtracted from gross plant in service to arrive at net utility plant in the rate base calculation. Sourced from SAP FI/CO asset accounting module.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Form 1

description: Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes (ADIT) balance that reduces the rate base. ADIT represents the cumulative timing differences between book and tax depreciation, which are treated as a cost-free source of capital that offsets the rate base per IRS normalization rules and FERC/PUC requirements.
reference: IRS Normalization Rules (IRC Section 168); FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 740 Income Taxes; FERC Form 1

business_glossary_term: Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) Rate
description: The Allowance for Funds Used During Construction (AFUDC) rate applied to Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) balances, expressed as a decimal. AFUDC represents the cost of financing capital projects during construction and is capitalized to the plant account per FERC Uniform System of Accounts.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: The authorized Return on Equity (ROE) rate approved by the regulatory commission for this rate case, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0950 for 9.50%). Used to calculate the equity return component of the revenue requirement in cost-of-service studies.
reference: State PUC Commission Order; FERC Order 679; FERC Form 1

description: The date on which the regulatory commission issued its final order approving the rate base for tariff purposes. Nullable until the commission issues its decision following the rate case proceeding.
reference: State PUC Commission Order; FERC Order

description: The embedded cost of long-term debt used in the capital structure for rate base return calculations, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.0450 for 4.50%). Calculated from the utility's outstanding long-term debt instruments as filed with the regulatory commission.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Cost-of-Capital Study; FERC Form 1

description: The timestamp when this rate base record was first created in the system, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides audit trail for record origination in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this rate base record. Typically USD for U.S. utility operations. Supports multi-currency reporting for utilities with cross-border operations.

Total customer deposit balances that reduce the rate base. Customer deposits are treated as a cost-free source of capital provided by customers, which offsets the utility's rate base investment in cost-of-service studies.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Cost-of-Service Study Methodology; FERC Form 1

description: Dollar value of capital projects currently under construction that are included in the rate base per regulatory authorization. CWIP inclusion in rate base is subject to PUC approval and AFUDC (Allowance for Funds Used During Construction) accounting treatment under FASB ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107; FERC Form 1

description: The proportion of long-term debt in the approved or proposed capital structure used for rate base return calculations, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5000 for 50%). Together with equity ratio, defines the capital structure for revenue requirement calculations.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Capital Structure Determination; FERC Form 1

description: The composite depreciation rate applied to utility plant in service for rate base and revenue requirement calculations, expressed as a decimal. Established through a depreciation study approved by the regulatory commission.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Depreciation Study Approval; FASB ASC 360

description: The date on which the approved rate base becomes effective for tariff and rate-setting purposes. Established by commission order following a General Rate Case (GRC) proceeding.
reference: State PUC Commission Order; FERC Form 1

description: The proportion of equity in the approved or proposed capital structure used for rate base return calculations, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.5000 for 50%). Determined by the regulatory commission in the rate case proceeding.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Capital Structure Determination; FERC Form 1

description: The date on which the approved rate base record expires or is superseded by a new rate case determination. Nullable for open-ended rate base records that remain in effect until a new rate case is filed.
reference: State PUC Commission Order; FERC Form 1

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: The FERC Uniform System of Accounts code associated with the primary plant account category driving this rate base record. Used for FERC Form 1 reporting and regulatory cost allocation studies.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The date on which the rate base data was formally filed with the regulatory commission (PUC or FERC) as part of the rate case application. Establishes the official record date for regulatory proceedings.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Filing Requirements; FERC Form 1 Annual Filing Deadline

description: Identifies the fuel or energy source type associated with generation plant assets included in this rate base record. Used for Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) reporting, Renewable Energy Certificate (REC) tracking, and environmental compliance cost allocation.
reference: EIA Form 860; FERC Form 1; State PUC Integrated Resource Plan (IRP) Filing Requirements

description: Total gross value of utility plant in service (before accumulated depreciation) included in the rate base calculation. Represents the original cost of all depreciable utility assets used and useful in providing regulated service, per FERC Uniform System of Accounts.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Utility Plant

business_glossary_term: Is Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) Included
description: Indicates whether Construction Work in Progress (CWIP) is included in the rate base (True) per regulatory authorization, or excluded (False) with AFUDC capitalized instead. CWIP inclusion requires specific PUC or FERC authorization.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC CWIP Authorization Orders

business_glossary_term: Is Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Jurisdictional
description: Indicates whether this rate base record falls under FERC jurisdiction (True) for interstate transmission and wholesale power sales, or under state PUC jurisdiction (False) for retail distribution and local gas distribution. Determines applicable regulatory accounting and reporting requirements.
reference: Federal Power Act Section 205/206; FERC Form 1; Natural Gas Act

description: Code identifying the regulatory jurisdiction (state or federal) under which this rate base record is filed. Used to segregate rate base components by PUC or FERC jurisdiction for cost-of-service studies and rate case filings.
reference: FERC Form 1; State Public Utility Commission (PUC) Filing Requirements

description: Net book value of utility plant in service, calculated as gross plant in service minus accumulated depreciation. Represents the primary component of the regulatory asset base (RAB) used in cost-of-service studies and Return on Equity (ROE) calculations.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: Free-text field for regulatory analysts and financial planners to document material adjustments, commission-ordered modifications, stipulations, or other explanatory notes associated with this rate base record. Supports audit trail and regulatory proceeding documentation.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Filing Requirements

description: Functional classification of the utility plant included in this rate base record per FERC Uniform System of Accounts. Distinguishes between generation, transmission, distribution, general plant, and intangible plant for cost allocation and rate design purposes.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The date as of which the utility plant in service balance is measured for inclusion in the rate base. Typically the last day of the test year or a specific date established by the regulatory commission for the cost-of-service study.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Test Year Definition; FERC Form 1

description: Externally-known business identifier for the rate base record, used in regulatory filings, cost-of-service studies, and rate case submissions to the Public Utility Commission (PUC). Typically formatted as a combination of jurisdiction code, rate class, and test year (e.g., CA-RES-2024).
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Filing Requirements

description: Current lifecycle status of the rate base record within the regulatory filing process. Tracks progression from internal draft preparation through regulatory filing, commission approval, and potential supersession by a subsequent rate case.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Procedural Rules; FERC Form 1

description: Official docket or case number assigned by the regulatory commission (PUC or FERC) to the rate case proceeding in which this rate base record is submitted. Used for regulatory tracking and cross-referencing with commission orders.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Filing Requirements; FERC Form 1

description: Code identifying the customer rate class (e.g., residential, commercial, industrial, agricultural) to which this rate base component is allocated. Supports cost-of-service allocation studies and rate design for General Rate Case (GRC) filings.
reference: State PUC Rate Schedule Tariffs; FERC Form 1

description: Total value of regulatory assets included in the rate base. Regulatory assets represent costs deferred for future recovery in rates as authorized by the PUC under FASB ASC 980, including deferred storm costs, deferred pension costs, and other commission-approved deferrals.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; State PUC Regulatory Asset Authorization Orders

description: Total value of regulatory liabilities that reduce the rate base. Regulatory liabilities represent obligations to return amounts to customers in future rates, such as excess deferred income taxes from tax reform or over-collected revenues, as authorized under FASB ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; IRS Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) Normalization Rules; State PUC Orders

description: The dollar amount of authorized return on the rate base, calculated as total rate base multiplied by the weighted average cost of capital (WACC). Represents the equity and debt return component of the revenue requirement.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Cost-of-Service Study; FERC Form 1

description: The total annual revenue requirement associated with this rate base record, representing the amount the utility is authorized to collect from customers to recover its costs and earn a fair return. Calculated as return on rate base plus operating expenses plus depreciation plus taxes.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Revenue Requirement Study; FERC Form 1

description: The SAP FI/CO cost center code associated with this rate base record, enabling linkage to the SAP ERP general ledger for financial reconciliation and cost-of-service allocation. Sourced from SAP Controlling (CO) module.
reference: SAP FI/CO Controlling Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The SAP Project System Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element code associated with capital projects contributing to this rate base record. Used to track CAPEX project costs from SAP PS module through to rate base inclusion.
reference: SAP Project System (PS) Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts Account 107 CWIP

description: Code identifying the geographic service territory or operating division to which this rate base record applies. Used for multi-territory utilities to allocate rate base components by service area for cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC Certificate of Public Convenience and Necessity (CPCN)

description: The calendar or fiscal year used as the basis for the rate case cost-of-service study. The test year establishes the period for which rate base, revenues, and expenses are measured to determine revenue requirements in a General Rate Case (GRC) filing.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Procedural Rules; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether the test year is based on historical actuals, a projected future period, or a hybrid combination of both. Regulatory commissions may require different test year types depending on jurisdiction rules.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Procedural Rules

description: Total regulatory asset base (RAB) amount, representing the net investment on which the utility is entitled to earn a return. Calculated as net utility plant plus CWIP plus working capital allowance plus regulatory assets minus regulatory liabilities minus ADIT minus customer deposits. Used as the basis for ROE and revenue requirement calculations in rate cases.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980; State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Filing Requirements; FERC Form 1

description: The timestamp when this rate base record was most recently modified, in ISO 8601 format (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Tracks the last update for data lineage, audit compliance, and change management in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; Internal Data Governance Policy

description: Identifies whether the rate base record pertains to the electric utility operations, natural gas utility operations, or a combined electric and gas utility. Supports separate rate base tracking for electric and gas jurisdictions.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Tariff Filing Requirements

business_glossary_term: Weighted Average Cost of Capital (WACC) Rate
description: The overall weighted average cost of capital (WACC) approved or proposed for this rate base, blending the cost of debt and equity weighted by their respective proportions in the capital structure. Used to calculate the total return on rate base in revenue requirement studies.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Cost-of-Service Study; FERC Form 1

description: Allowance for working capital included in the rate base, representing the utility's investment in cash and materials needed to operate between billing cycles. Typically calculated using the lead-lag method or a fixed percentage of operating expenses as approved by the PUC.
reference: State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Cost-of-Service Study Methodology; FERC Form 1

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each regulatory asset or regulatory liability record in the FASB ASC 980 ledger. Primary key for this data product.
Foreign key linking to finance.cost_center. Business justification: Regulatory Asset needs direct link to Cost Center for allocation tracking.
Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Regulatory Asset needs direct links to GL Account and Cost Center for regulatory reporting.

Reference to the capital project in the capital project accounting system (SAP PS) that originated the costs deferred into this regulatory asset. Enables traceability from the regulatory asset balance back to the underlying CAPEX project for rate base and depreciation analysis.
reference: SAP FI/CO Project System (PS); FERC Form 1 CWIP Schedule

description: Reference to the capital project in the capital project accounting system (SAP PS) that originated the costs deferred into this regulatory asset. Enables traceability from the regulatory asset balance back to the underlying CAPEX project for rate base and depreciation analysis.
reference: SAP FI/CO Project System (PS); FERC Form 1 CWIP Schedule

description: The fiscal accounting period (YYYY-MM) to which the current balance and amortization figures apply. Used for period-end close reporting, FERC Form 1 annual filing, and SAP FI/CO period-end postings.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; SAP FI/CO Period-End Close

description: The cumulative carrying charges (interest on the deferred balance) accrued on this regulatory asset or liability to date (in USD). Included in the total balance subject to recovery or refund through rates.
reference: FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Form 1

description: The method prescribed by the authorizing rate order for amortizing this regulatory asset or liability. 'straight_line' is most common; 'regulatory_prescribed' indicates a custom schedule mandated by the regulator; 'units_of_production' may apply to fuel-related deferrals.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Rate Orders

description: The annual dollar amount authorized for amortization (recovery or refund) of this regulatory asset or liability through customer rates (in USD). Derived from the approved amortization schedule in the rate order. Used for budgeting and CAPEX/OPEX tracking.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Form 1

description: Name or employee identifier of the finance officer or regulatory accounting manager who approved the creation or material modification of this regulatory asset record. Required for SOX Section 302/404 internal controls over financial reporting.
reference: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 302 and 404; FASB ASC 980

description: Descriptive human-readable name of the regulatory asset or liability (e.g., 'Deferred Storm Restoration Costs', 'Pension Regulatory Asset', 'Fuel Adjustment Clause Deferral'). Used in financial statements and rate case testimony.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Regulatory Assets and Liabilities

description: Externally-known alphanumeric identifier assigned by the finance or regulatory accounting team to uniquely reference this regulatory asset or liability in rate case filings, FERC Form 1 schedules, and SAP FI/CO postings. Serves as the business-facing key across systems.
reference: FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980; SAP FI/CO

description: Indicates whether this record represents a regulatory asset (costs deferred for future recovery from ratepayers) or a regulatory liability (obligations deferred for future refund to ratepayers) under FASB ASC 980.

The date on which the regulatory commission issued the rate order or decision authorizing the creation of this regulatory asset or liability. Establishes the FASB ASC 980 recognition date and the legal basis for deferral accounting.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-25; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Orders

description: The regulatory jurisdiction that authorized this regulatory asset or liability — Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for interstate transmission, state Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Public Service Commission (PSC) for distribution, or both for dual-jurisdiction items.

The opening balance of the regulatory asset or liability at the start of the current accounting period (in USD). Used as the baseline for amortization calculations and period-over-period variance analysis in FERC Form 1 and rate case filings.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Regulatory Assets; FASB ASC 230

description: Indicates whether this regulatory asset is classified as a capital expenditure (CAPEX) item on the balance sheet (True) or an operating expenditure (OPEX) deferral (False). Affects rate base inclusion, depreciation treatment, and EBITDA reporting under FASB ASC 980 and FASB ASC 360.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FASB ASC 360 — Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Form 1

description: The authorized carrying charge (interest) rate applied to the unamortized balance of this regulatory asset or liability between the deferral date and the recovery start date, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.060000 for 6.0%). Compensates the utility for the time value of money on deferred costs.
reference: FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Form 1

description: The timestamp when this regulatory asset record was first created in the system (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Provides the audit trail creation event for SOX compliance and data lineage tracking.
reference: FASB ASC 980; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 404; SAP FI/CO Audit Log

description: Total amortization recognized to date against this regulatory asset or liability since its inception (in USD). Represents the portion already recovered from or refunded to ratepayers through rates. Used to reconcile the original authorized amount to the current balance.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35; FERC Form 1; SAP FI/CO Asset Accounting

description: The current outstanding balance of the regulatory asset or liability as of the most recent accounting period close (in USD). Represents the net unamortized amount remaining for future recovery or refund through rates. Core field for RAB valuation and EBITDA reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; SAP FI/CO Balance Sheet

description: The date on which costs or obligations began to be deferred into this regulatory asset or liability account. May differ from the authorization date if the regulator authorized retroactive deferral. Used for amortization period calculations.
reference: FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Orders

description: Indicates whether this regulatory asset carries a risk of partial or full disallowance by the regulator (True = at risk; False = recovery considered probable). Under FASB ASC 980, if recovery is no longer probable, the asset must be written off. Used for financial risk management and disclosure.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35-1; SEC Disclosure Requirements; State PUC Proceedings

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Number
description: The FERC Uniform System of Accounts account number to which this regulatory asset or liability is classified (e.g., Account 182.3 for Other Regulatory Assets, Account 254 for Other Regulatory Liabilities, Account 283 for Deferred Income Taxes). Required for FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Form 1 Schedule
description: The specific FERC Form 1 schedule or page reference where this regulatory asset or liability is reported (e.g., 'Schedule 232 — Regulatory Assets', 'Schedule 278 — Regulatory Liabilities'). Supports automated FERC Form 1 report generation.

The deferred income tax amount associated with this regulatory asset or liability (in USD), arising from temporary differences between book and tax treatment of the deferred costs. Required for FASB ASC 740 and ASC 980 interaction disclosures and FERC Form 1 tax normalization schedules.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FASB ASC 740 — Income Taxes; FERC Form 1 Tax Normalization

description: The date of the most recent regulatory commission review, audit, or order affecting this regulatory asset or liability. Used to track compliance with ongoing regulatory reporting obligations and to identify assets due for re-authorization.
reference: State PUC Audit Requirements; FERC Compliance Filings

description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this regulatory asset record (yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.SSSXXX). Used for change tracking, SOX audit compliance, and incremental data pipeline processing in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 404; SAP FI/CO Change Log; FASB ASC 980

description: The scheduled date of the next regulatory commission review or rate case proceeding in which this regulatory asset or liability will be examined. Used for proactive regulatory compliance planning and rate case preparation.
reference: State PUC Rate Case Schedules; FERC Compliance Calendar

description: The total dollar amount of costs or obligations originally authorized by the regulator for deferral and future recovery or refund (in USD). Establishes the ceiling for the regulatory asset or liability as approved in the rate order.
reference: FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Orders

description: Narrative description of the business event or circumstance that gave rise to this regulatory asset or liability (e.g., 'Hurricane Ida storm restoration costs incurred Q3 2021', 'Pension obligation increase due to actuarial assumption change', 'Nuclear decommissioning cost deferral per Order No. 2023-14'). Supports audit trails and rate case testimony.
reference: FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Orders

description: The utility plant function to which this regulatory asset or liability is associated, used for jurisdictional allocation and rate class assignment in cost-of-service studies. Aligns with FERC functional classification for T&D separation.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FERC Form 1; State PUC Cost-of-Service Study

description: Management's assessment of the probability that this regulatory asset will be recovered through future rates, using the FASB ASC 450 contingency framework. 'probable' supports continued recognition; 'reasonably_possible' or 'remote' may trigger impairment or write-off under ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35; FASB ASC 450 — Contingencies; SEC MD&A Disclosure

description: The official docket or case number assigned by the state Public Utility Commission (PUC) or Public Service Commission (PSC) authorizing the deferral or recovery of this regulatory asset or liability. Essential for regulatory compliance tracking and rate case filings.
reference: State PUC/PSC Rate Orders; FERC Docket System

description: Indicates whether this regulatory asset is included in the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) for rate-of-return calculations. True if the asset earns a return on investment in the rate base; False if it is a non-earning deferral. Critical for Return on Equity (ROE) and rate case calculations.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; GRC Rate Base Schedule

description: Reference to the General Rate Case (GRC) or rate proceeding in which this regulatory asset or liability was established or most recently reviewed. Used to link financial records to the regulatory proceeding for cost-of-service study support and rate case testimony.
reference: State PUC GRC Filing Requirements; FERC Rate Case Procedures

description: The specific rate order or commission order number issued by the PUC, PSC, or FERC that authorizes the creation, recovery, or refund of this regulatory asset or liability. Provides the legal basis for FASB ASC 980 recognition.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-25-1; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Orders

description: The scheduled date on which full amortization (recovery or refund) of this regulatory asset or liability is expected to be completed. Defines the end of the authorized recovery period. Nullable for open-ended or indefinite-term regulatory assets.
reference: FASB ASC 980-340-35; State PUC Rate Orders; FERC Form 1

description: The rate mechanism through which this regulatory asset is recovered from customers or the regulatory liability is refunded to customers. description: Unique surrogate identifier for each accounts receivable transaction record in the finance domain. Primary key for the ar_transaction data product.
reference: FASB ASC 310 – Receivables; SAP FI-AR Module

description: Reference to the underlying commercial contract, Power Purchase Agreement (PPA), transmission service agreement, or inter-company agreement that governs this AR transaction. Links to the contract master for terms and pricing validation.
reference: FERC Form 1; Allegro ETRM Contract Module; FASB ASC 606

description: Reference to the SAP CO cost center responsible for the revenue stream associated with this AR transaction. Used for internal cost-of-service allocation and rate case studies.

Reference to the counterparty (customer, wholesale buyer, inter-company entity, or transmission service customer) that owes the receivable. Maps to the SAP FI-AR customer account (KUNNR) for non-retail revenue streams including wholesale energy, REC sales, and FERC-jurisdictional wheeling charges.
Foreign key linking to property.facility. Business justification: Revenue from customers served by a specific facility is tracked per facility for performance reporting.

Reference to the general ledger account to which this AR transaction is posted. Determines the revenue or receivable classification in the chart of accounts for FERC Form 1 reporting and FASB ASC 980 regulatory accounting.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; SAP FI-GL

description: Foreign key linking to property.parcel. Business justification: Revenue transactions are associated with service parcels to support revenue analysis and rate‑case filings.

Net value of credits, discounts, or billing corrections applied to this AR transaction after initial invoicing. Negative values represent credits issued to the counterparty; positive values represent additional charges. Supports dispute resolution and revenue true-up processes.
reference: FASB ASC 606; SAP FI-AR Credit Memo

description: Aging classification of the outstanding AR balance based on the number of days past the due date. Used for bad debt provisioning, collection prioritization, and AR aging reports required for FERC Form 1 and internal financial reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 310-10-50; FERC Form 1; SAP FI-AR Aging Report

description: SAP organizational unit code identifying the business unit (e.g., Electric Transmission, Gas Distribution, Generation) responsible for the revenue stream associated with this AR transaction. Used for segment reporting and FERC Form 1 functional classification.
reference: SAP FI Organizational Structure; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 280 – Segment Reporting

description: SAP FI-AR clearing document number assigned when this AR transaction is fully or partially settled against an incoming payment. Enables reconciliation between the AR open item and the corresponding bank receipt or inter-company settlement.

External contract or agreement reference number (e.g., PPA number, transmission service agreement number, FERC tariff rate schedule reference) associated with this AR transaction. Used for counterparty reconciliation without requiring a join to the contract master.
reference: FERC Form 1; Allegro ETRM; FASB ASC 606

description: Classification of the counterparty category for this AR transaction. Distinguishes wholesale energy buyers, inter-company entities, RTO/ISO settlement parties, transmission service customers, REC buyers, and miscellaneous non-retail receivables. Drives reporting segmentation for FERC Form 1 and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980; SAP FI-AR

description: Timestamp when this AR transaction record was first created in the system of record (SAP FI-AR). Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI Audit Log

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this AR transaction (e.g., USD for US Dollar). Supports multi-currency reporting for cross-border wholesale energy transactions and PPA settlements.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 830 – Foreign Currency

description: Number of calendar days elapsed since the payment due date for overdue AR transactions. Zero or negative values indicate the transaction is current. Used for collection escalation triggers and bad debt reserve calculations.

Indicates whether the counterparty has formally disputed this AR transaction. True = active dispute in progress; False = no dispute. Triggers dispute management workflow and suspends dunning activity in SAP FI-AR.
reference: SAP FI-AR Dispute Management; FASB ASC 310

description: Categorized reason code for the counterparty dispute on this AR transaction. Used for dispute root cause analysis and resolution tracking. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: billing_error|quantity_dispute|price_dispute|service_not_rendered|contract_terms|duplicate_invoice|other — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP FI-AR Dispute Management; FASB ASC 310

description: Contractual date by which the counterparty is required to remit payment for this AR transaction. Basis for aging bucket assignment, overdue status determination, and late payment interest calculations per contract terms.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR Payment Terms (ZTERM)

description: Date on which the most recent dunning (collection notice) was issued to the counterparty for this AR transaction. Used to enforce dunning intervals and track collection activity history.

Current dunning (collection notice) level assigned to this AR transaction in SAP FI-AR, ranging from 0 (no dunning) to the maximum configured level. Higher levels indicate escalating collection actions. Used to track collection effort intensity.

Quantity of electrical energy in Megawatt-Hours (MWh) associated with this AR transaction for wholesale energy sales, RTO/ISO settlements, or PPA deliveries. Null for non-energy revenue streams such as REC sales or inter-company charges.

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts code applicable to this AR transaction for regulatory financial reporting. Required for FERC Form 1 electric and gas revenue classification (e.g., Account 440 – Sales of Electricity, Account 456 – Other Electric Revenues).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: Fiscal accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year in which this AR transaction is posted. Aligns with SAP FI posting period (MONAT) for period-end close and regulatory reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 606; FERC Form 1; SAP FI MONAT

description: Fiscal year in which this AR transaction is recognized for financial reporting purposes. Used for period-end close, FERC Form 1 annual reporting, and EBITDA analysis. Aligns with the SAP FI posting period (GJAHR).
reference: FASB ASC 606; FERC Form 1; SAP FI GJAHR

description: Indicates whether this AR transaction represents an inter-company charge between affiliated entities within the utility holding company structure. True = inter-company; False = third-party. Required for inter-company elimination in consolidated financial statements.
reference: FASB ASC 810 – Consolidation; SAP FI Inter-Company Reconciliation

description: Gross billed amount on the AR invoice before any adjustments, credits, or taxes. Represents the total amount owed by the counterparty at the time of invoice issuance. Denominated in the currency specified by currency_code.
reference: FASB ASC 606; FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR

description: Externally-known invoice document number assigned to this AR transaction, used for counterparty reconciliation and audit trail. Corresponds to the SAP FI-AR document number (BELNR) for non-retail receivables such as wholesale energy sales, FERC wheeling charges, and inter-company settlements.
reference: SAP FI-AR BELNR; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 310

description: Locational Marginal Price (LMP) in $/MWh used to value wholesale energy transactions settled through the RTO/ISO Day-Ahead Market (DAM) or Real-Time Market (RTM). Sourced from the applicable RTO/ISO settlement statement.
reference: FERC Order 2000; RTO/ISO Settlement Statements; Allegro ETRM

description: Net receivable amount after applying all adjustments and taxes to the invoice amount (invoice_amount + tax_amount + adjustment_amount). Represents the actual amount expected to be collected from the counterparty. Used for aging analysis and collection reporting.

Remaining unpaid balance on this AR transaction (net_amount minus paid_amount). Represents the current exposure for collection management and bad debt provisioning. Refreshed upon each payment or adjustment posting.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR Open Item Management

description: Cumulative amount received from the counterparty against this AR transaction to date. Used to calculate the outstanding balance and determine partial payment status. Updated upon each payment posting in SAP FI-AR.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR Payment Posting

description: Date on which full or final payment was received and posted for this AR transaction. Null if the transaction remains open or partially paid. Used for cash flow reporting and days sales outstanding (DSO) analysis.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR Clearing Date

description: SAP payment terms key (e.g., NT30, NT45, NT60) defining the contractual payment schedule, discount periods, and due date calculation rules for this AR transaction. Drives automated due date computation in SAP FI-AR.

Reference to the applicable General Rate Case (GRC) or FERC rate case docket number under which the revenue rate for this AR transaction was authorized. Used for cost-of-service study support and regulatory compliance documentation.
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC GRC Filings; FASB ASC 980

description: Number of Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) sold and invoiced in this AR transaction. One REC represents one MWh of electricity generated from a qualifying renewable source. Applicable only to REC sales revenue streams.
reference: EPA Green Power Partnership; State RPS Requirements; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether this AR transaction is associated with a FERC or state PUC-approved regulatory asset or deferred revenue mechanism under FASB ASC 980. True = subject to regulatory accounting treatment; False = standard commercial receivable.
reference: FASB ASC 980 – Regulated Operations; FERC Form 1; State PUC Orders

description: Business classification of the revenue type driving this AR transaction. Supports segmented revenue reporting for FERC Form 1, rate case cost-of-service studies, and EBITDA analysis. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: wholesale_energy_sales|transmission_wheeling|rec_sales|intercompany_charge|ppa_settlement|ancillary_services|miscellaneous — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 606; FASB ASC 980

description: End date of the billing period or service delivery period covered by this AR transaction. Paired with service_period_start to define the revenue recognition window under FASB ASC 606.
reference: FASB ASC 606; FERC Form 1; SAP FI-AR

description: Start date of the billing period or service delivery period covered by this AR transaction. For wholesale energy sales, this is the start of the energy delivery interval. For transmission wheeling, it is the start of the reservation period. Required for revenue recognition under FASB ASC 606.
reference: FASB ASC 606; FERC Form 1; SAP FI-AR

description: Total tax charges applied to this AR transaction, including applicable state and federal taxes on wholesale energy sales or transmission services. Part of the monetary triplet supporting net amount calculation.
reference: FASB ASC 740; SAP FI-AR Tax Determination

description: The principal business event date on which the AR transaction was originated — i.e., the date the revenue was earned or the invoice was issued. Used as the basis for aging calculations and revenue recognition under FASB ASC 606.
reference: FASB ASC 606 – Revenue Recognition; SAP FI-AR Posting Date

description: Current lifecycle state of the AR transaction indicating collection progress. Open = unpaid and within terms; partially_paid = partial payment received; paid = fully settled; overdue = past due date; disputed = counterparty has raised a formal dispute; written_off = deemed uncollectible and removed from active AR.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI-AR Status Management

description: RTO/ISO transmission pricing zone or load zone associated with this AR transaction for wheeling charges and transmission service revenues. Used for FERC-jurisdictional revenue allocation and FERC Form 1 reporting.

Timestamp of the most recent modification to this AR transaction record, including status changes, payment postings, dispute updates, or write-off actions. Supports change data capture in the Databricks Silver layer.
reference: FASB ASC 310; SAP FI Audit Log

description: Amount written off as uncollectible for this AR transaction. May be less than the full outstanding balance if a partial write-off was applied. Used for bad debt reserve reconciliation and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 310-10; FERC Form 1; SAP FI-AR

description: Date on which this AR transaction was written off as uncollectible and the bad debt expense was recognized. Null if the transaction has not been written off. Required for FASB ASC 310 impairment disclosure.
reference: FASB ASC 310-10; SAP FI-AR Write-Off Posting

description: Indicates whether this AR transaction has been written off as uncollectible. True = written off and removed from active AR; False = still active. Triggers bad debt expense recognition under FASB ASC 310-10.
reference: FASB ASC 310-10 – Receivables Impairment; SAP FI-AR Write-Off

Unique surrogate identifier for each SAP FI automatic payment program run record in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Primary key for this entity.
reference: SAP FI Payment Program (F110); FASB ASC 230 Statement of Cash Flows

description: SAP user ID of the supervisor or treasury manager who approved the payment proposal before posting. Enforces dual-control requirements for disbursements above threshold amounts per internal controls policy.
reference: SOX Section 404 Dual Control; SAP FI Authorization Objects; Internal AP Controls Policy

description: SAP FI bank account identifier (account ID within the house bank) from which disbursements are made. Identifies the specific checking or disbursement account used for this payment run. Classified confidential due to financial account sensitivity.
reference: SAP FI House Bank Account Configuration; PCI DSS; Treasury Cash Management

description: Reference to the primary SAP CO cost center associated with this payment run, used for OPEX allocation and cost-of-service studies. Relevant for payment runs covering operational expenditures such as fuel procurement, O&M vendor payments, and workforce expenses.
reference: SAP CO Cost Center Accounting; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; Rate Case Cost-of-Service Studies

description: SAP user ID of the AP/treasury staff member who initiated (scheduled or executed) the payment run in SAP F110. Required for segregation-of-duties controls and SOX audit trail.
reference: SAP FI F110 User Log; SOX Section 404 Segregation of Duties; NERC CIP-004 Personnel

description: Reference to the primary GL clearing account used for this payment run's disbursements (e.g., bank clearing account, outgoing payment account). Supports general ledger reconciliation and FERC account mapping.
reference: SAP FI Chart of Accounts; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 230

description: SAP FI house bank identifier representing the utility's internal bank master record from which payments are disbursed. Links to the specific bank account used for this payment run, supporting bank reconciliation and cash position reporting.
reference: SAP FI House Bank Configuration (FI12); Treasury Cash Management

description: Foreign key linking to trading.trading_portfolio. Business justification: Supports Payment Run Settlement Report linking payments to the trading portfolio that generated the settlement obligations.

Reference to the original payment_run_id that this run reverses, if reversal_flag is True. Enables traceability between reversal runs and their originating payment runs for audit and reconciliation purposes.
reference: SAP FI Payment Reversal; FASB ASC 230; Internal Audit Trail

description: Date and time when the payment proposal was approved by the authorized approver. Supports segregation-of-duties audit trail and turnaround time analysis for AP processing efficiency.
reference: SOX Section 404; SAP FI Workflow Approval Log; Internal AP Controls

description: Masked representation of the utility's disbursement bank account number, showing only the last four digits for identification and reconciliation purposes without exposing the full account number. Used in audit reports and bank reconciliation statements.
reference: PCI DSS Requirement 3.4; SAP FI Bank Master Data; FASB ASC 230

description: Indicates whether the payment medium file (e.g., ACH NACHA file, SWIFT MT103, check print file) was successfully generated and transmitted to the bank for this payment run. False indicates a file generation failure requiring investigation.
reference: SAP FI Payment Medium Workbench (PMW); NACHA ACH File Format; SWIFT Standards

description: Date and time when the payment medium file was transmitted to the bank or payment processor. Used for bank reconciliation cutoff determination and exception investigation when payments are not reflected in bank statements.
reference: SAP FI Payment Medium Workbench; NACHA ACH Transmission Rules; Treasury Operations

description: American Bankers Association (ABA) routing transit number of the utility's disbursement bank. Required for ACH and wire payment file generation and bank reconciliation. Nine-digit numeric code.
reference: NACHA ACH Operating Rules; Federal Reserve Regulation J; ABA Routing Number Standard

description: Indicates whether the disbursements in this payment run are classified as capital expenditures (CAPEX), operating expenditures (OPEX), or a mix of both. Critical for regulatory asset base (RAB) valuation, rate case cost-of-service studies, and FERC Form 1 plant account reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FASB ASC 980; Rate Case Cost-of-Service Studies

description: Timestamp when this payment run record was first captured in the Silver Layer lakehouse. Supports data lineage, audit trail, and record management.
reference: FASB ASC 230; SOX Section 404 Audit Trail Requirements; NIST SP 800-53 Audit and Accountability

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this payment run (e.g., 'USD'). Utility operations are predominantly USD; this field supports multi-currency scenarios for cross-border energy trading settlements or foreign vendor payments.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency

description: Total cash discount amount captured across all payment documents in this run, representing early payment discounts (e.g., 2/10 net 30 terms) taken from vendor invoices. Reduces the net payment amount and is posted to a discount revenue GL account.
reference: SAP FI Cash Discount Processing; FASB ASC 835 Interest; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: SAP F110 parameter specifying the latest document entry date for invoices to be considered in this payment run. Ensures only invoices entered into SAP by this cutoff date are included, supporting period-close controls.
reference: SAP FI F110 Selection Parameters; Period-Close Controls

description: Total number of individual payment documents (FI payment postings) generated by this payment run. Each document represents a payment to a single vendor or employee. Used for run validation, exception monitoring, and audit completeness checks.
reference: SAP FI F110 Payment Run Log; Internal Audit Controls

description: Number of vendor invoices or payment items that were excluded from this payment run due to exceptions (e.g., payment block, missing bank details, duplicate invoice flag, credit hold). Drives AP exception resolution workflow.
reference: SAP FI F110 Exception Log; Accounts Payable Controls; Internal Audit

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts code associated with the primary expenditure category of this payment run (e.g., Account 920 for administrative salaries, Account 151 for fuel stock). Supports FERC Form 1 regulatory reporting and rate case cost allocation.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP FI fiscal period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–13 for 13-period calendars) within the fiscal year in which this payment run is posted. Supports period-close cash disbursement reporting and budget-to-actual variance analysis.
reference: SAP FI Fiscal Period Configuration; FERC Form 1 Monthly Reporting

description: SAP FI fiscal year in which this payment run's disbursements are recorded. Used for annual financial reporting, FERC Form 1 filing, and CAPEX/OPEX budget variance analysis.
reference: SAP FI Fiscal Year Configuration; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: Total gross disbursement amount for all payment documents included in this payment run before application of discounts or deductions. Represents the sum of all vendor invoice and expense reimbursement amounts selected for payment. Used for cash flow forecasting and bank reconciliation.
reference: FASB ASC 230 Statement of Cash Flows; FERC Form 1 Disbursements; SAP FI F110

description: Total number of vendor invoices and expense reimbursement line items cleared (paid) by this payment run. A single payment document may clear multiple invoices; this count reflects the total open items settled.
reference: SAP FI Open Item Management; Accounts Payable Controls; FERC Form 1

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this payment run record in the Silver Layer. Tracks status changes, corrections, and reversals for audit and data quality monitoring.
reference: SOX Section 404; NIST SP 800-53; SAP FI Change Document Log

description: Net total amount actually disbursed in this payment run after deducting cash discounts and other adjustments from the gross payment amount. This is the actual cash outflow recorded in the treasury cash position and bank statement.
reference: FASB ASC 230 Statement of Cash Flows; SAP FI F110 Payment Run Summary; FERC Form 1

description: The 'next payment date' parameter used in the SAP F110 payment proposal to determine which open invoices are due for payment. Invoices with a due date on or before this date are selected for inclusion in the run.
reference: SAP FI F110 Selection Parameters; Accounts Payable Payment Terms

description: Free-text notes entered by the AP/treasury team describing special circumstances, exceptions, or instructions for this payment run (e.g., 'Emergency payment for critical grid equipment supplier', 'Held pending PO approval'). Supports operational communication and audit documentation.
reference: SAP FI F110 Notes Field; Internal AP Controls

description: SAP FI company code of the legal entity initiating the payment run. For a utility with multiple regulated subsidiaries (electric vs. gas), this identifies which legal entity's bank account and chart of accounts are used. Aligns with FERC jurisdictional entity reporting.
reference: SAP FI Company Code Configuration; FERC Form 1 Entity Identification; FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations

description: SAP FI payment method code indicating the instrument used to disburse funds (e.g., ACH for Automated Clearing House, CHECK for paper check, WIRE for wire transfer, EFT for electronic funds transfer). Drives bank file format generation and clearing account determination.
reference: SAP FI Payment Method Configuration (FBZP); NACHA ACH Rules; Federal Reserve Wire Transfer Regulations
