reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; SAP FI/CO

description: SAP CO functional area code classifying the nature of the cost (e.g., production, administration, sales, R&D). Used for income statement reporting by function and FERC Form 1 functional classification of utility costs.
reference: SAP CO Module; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The SAP FI general ledger account code to which the allocated cost is posted. Aligns with the FERC Uniform System of Accounts (e.g., Account 920 for administrative and general salaries, Account 921 for office supplies). Critical for FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SAP FI/CO; FASB ASC 980

description: Indicates whether this allocation crosses legal entity boundaries (True = inter-company allocation between affiliates in a utility holding company). Inter-company allocations require additional regulatory scrutiny under FERC affiliate transaction rules and state PUC standards.
reference: FERC Affiliate Transaction Rules; SAP FI/CO; PUC Rate Case Standards

description: Code identifying the regulatory jurisdiction (e.g., state abbreviation or FERC) to which the allocated cost is attributable. Critical for multi-jurisdictional utilities to separate costs for individual state PUC rate cases and FERC wholesale rate filings.
reference: FERC; State PUC Rate Case Standards; FASB ASC 980

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this cost allocation record, including reversals, corrections, or status changes. Supports incremental data loading and change tracking in the lakehouse.
The date on which the cost allocation was posted to the SAP CO ledger. This is the principal business event date used for period assignment and financial reporting.
reference: SAP FI/CO; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: Reference number of the General Rate Case (GRC) or FERC rate proceeding for which this allocation is being tracked. Enables direct linkage of cost allocation records to specific regulatory filings and cost-of-service studies.

SAP CO profit center code receiving the allocated costs when receiver_type is 'profit_center'. Used for segment-level profitability reporting and inter-company allocations in multi-jurisdictional utility structures.

Discriminator indicating the type of SAP CO object receiving the allocated costs: cost_center (another cost center), profit_center (a profit center for segment reporting), wbs_element (a capital project WBS element for CAPEX tracking), or internal_order.

business_glossary_term: Receiver Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) Element Code
description: SAP PS Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element code receiving allocated costs when receiver_type is 'wbs_element'. Used for CAPEX project cost tracking, regulatory asset base (RAB) valuation, and CPCN project accounting.
reference: SAP CO/PS Module; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether the allocated cost contributes to a regulatory asset or liability as defined under FASB ASC 980 (Regulated Operations). True when the allocation feeds a deferred cost that is recoverable through future rates approved by the PUC or FERC.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; PUC Rate Case Standards

description: The date on which the reversal of this allocation was posted in SAP CO. Null when no reversal exists. Used for period-end close reconciliation and audit trail.
SAP CO document number of the reversal posting if this allocation has been reversed. Null when no reversal exists. Used for audit trail and period-end reconciliation.

Indicates whether the allocation was executed against actual costs, planned/budget costs, or as a simulation. 'actual' postings feed financial statements; 'plan' allocations support budgeting and CAPEX/OPEX planning; 'simulation' records are not posted to the ledger.

The total cost balance of the sender cost center prior to allocation for the fiscal period. Used to verify that the sum of all allocated_amount values equals the sender's total cost, ensuring full cost recovery in the allocation cycle.
reference: SAP CO Module; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: Classifies the allocated cost by utility function per FERC Uniform System of Accounts: generation, transmission, distribution, gas distribution, common (shared across functions), or corporate. Directly supports cost-of-service studies and rate case filings.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; PUC Rate Case Standards; FASB ASC 980

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the cost center or internal order record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this entity.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master Data

description: Foreign key linking to property.facility. Business justification: Cost centers are assigned to facilities to allocate operating expenses per building or plant.
Foreign key linking to property.parcel. Business justification: Cost centers are organized by geographic parcels for OPEX reporting and internal cost allocation.
FK to finance.profit_center

SAP CO activity type code associated with this cost center, defining the type of work or service output (e.g., labor hours, machine hours, kWh produced). Activity types are used to calculate activity prices and allocate costs to cost objects such as maintenance orders and capital projects.

The statistical or activity-based basis used to allocate costs from this cost center (e.g., headcount, floor area, kWh consumed, labor hours). Used in overhead cost allocation cycles and cost-of-service studies to distribute shared costs equitably across cost objects and customer classes.
reference: SAP FI/CO Statistical Key Figures; FERC Cost Allocation Methodology

description: SAP CO allocation method used to distribute costs from this cost center to other cost objects. 'direct' posts costs directly; 'assessment' uses assessment cycles to allocate overhead; 'distribution' reallocates primary costs; 'periodic_reposting' corrects mispostings. Drives month-end cost closing procedures.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Allocation Configuration; Activity-Based Costing (ABC)

description: Approved annual OPEX budget amount for this cost center in the controlling currency. Represents the authorized spending limit for operations and maintenance activities. Used in budget variance analysis, rate case cost-of-service studies, and EBITDA reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1; Internal Budget Management Policy

description: The fiscal year (four-digit integer, e.g., 2025) to which the annual OPEX budget applies. Aligns with the utility's regulatory fiscal year for rate case filings and FERC Form 1 annual reporting.
reference: SAP FI/CO Fiscal Year Variant; FERC Form 1

description: SAP Business Area code representing a distinct area of operations for internal balance sheet and P&L reporting. For utilities, commonly used to separate electric, gas, and corporate segments for regulatory reporting and FERC jurisdictional cost separation.
reference: SAP FI/CO Business Area; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: SAP company code representing the legal entity or regulated subsidiary to which this cost center is assigned. Used for statutory financial reporting, FERC Form 1 filing, and separation of electric vs. gas utility accounts per regulatory requirements.
reference: SAP FI/CO Company Code; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP Controlling Area code to which this cost center belongs. The controlling area defines the organizational unit within which cost accounting is performed. For a utility, typically maps to the legal entity or regulated operating company (e.g., electric vs. gas utility segment).
reference: SAP FI/CO Controlling Area Configuration; FERC Form 1

description: SAP CO cost center category code that controls which activity types and statistical key figures can be posted. Common utility categories include E (Energy/Production), F (Field Operations), G (General Administration), V (Service/Overhead). Drives cost allocation rules and activity rate calculations. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: E|F|G|V|P|I|H|D — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Category Configuration

description: The externally-known alphanumeric code assigned to the cost center in SAP CO, used across all financial transactions, journal entries, and cost allocations. Serves as the business identifier referenced in FERC Form 1 reporting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master; FERC Form 1

description: Long-form textual description of the cost center's purpose, scope, and organizational context. Provides additional detail beyond the short name for use in financial reports, rate case documentation, and audit support.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master; FERC Form 1

description: Human-readable descriptive name of the cost center (e.g., 'Transmission District 3 Operations', 'Nuclear Generation Plant A', 'Storm Restoration Pool'). Used in financial reports, budget presentations, and rate case filings.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master; FASB ASC 980

description: Current lifecycle status of the cost center. 'active' indicates the cost center is open for postings; 'locked' prevents new postings while retaining history; 'closed' indicates the cost center has been decommissioned. Controls whether financial transactions can be posted against this cost center in SAP CO.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master; FASB ASC 980

description: Classifies whether this record represents a permanent cost center (e.g., generation plant, T&D district, corporate function) or a temporary cost collector such as an internal order for maintenance jobs, storm restoration events, or overhead pools. Drives allocation logic and reporting treatment. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: permanent|internal_order|overhead_pool|storm_restoration|project_collector — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Category; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Timestamp when this cost center master record was first created in the source system (SAP CO). Supports audit trail requirements, data lineage tracking, and compliance with NERC CIP and FASB record retention requirements.
reference: SAP FI/CO Audit Trail; FASB ASC 980; NERC CIP-003

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the cost center's controlling currency (e.g., 'USD'). Defines the currency in which budgets, actual costs, and variances are recorded and reported for this cost center.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP FI/CO Controlling Area Currency

description: Organizational department code to which this cost center is assigned. Supports departmental budgeting, OPEX tracking, and organizational reporting. Aligns with the utility's organizational chart and workforce management structure.
reference: SAP FI/CO Organizational Structure; Internal Organizational Chart

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USofA) account code associated with this cost center for regulatory financial reporting. Maps cost center expenditures to the prescribed FERC account structure required for Form 1 filing (e.g., Account 580 for Operation Supervision and Engineering - Transmission).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts for Public Utilities; FERC Form 1

description: SAP Functional Area code used to classify costs by business function (e.g., Generation, Transmission, Distribution, Customer Service, Administration) for cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1 functional reporting requirements.
reference: SAP FI/CO Functional Area; FERC Form 1 Functional Classification

description: Code identifying the cost center group (hierarchy node) to which this cost center belongs in the SAP CO standard hierarchy. Supports hierarchical OPEX reporting, departmental budgeting roll-ups, and organizational cost aggregation for rate case filings.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Group / Standard Hierarchy

description: Numeric level of this cost center within the SAP CO standard hierarchy (e.g., 1=Corporate, 2=Division, 3=Department, 4=Work Group). Supports hierarchical roll-up reporting for OPEX budgeting and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP FI/CO Standard Hierarchy; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether this cost center (or internal order) is used as a capital project cost collector for CAPEX tracking. When True, costs are subject to capitalization rules under FASB ASC 360 and are tracked for inclusion in the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB) for rate case filings.
reference: FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether costs accumulated in this cost center qualify as a regulatory asset under FASB ASC 980 (Regulated Operations). When True, deferred costs are expected to be recovered through future rate cases and are tracked for RAB valuation and ROE calculations.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; State PUC Rate Case Requirements

description: Indicates whether this cost center is designated for storm restoration cost capture. When True, costs posted here are tracked separately for regulatory recovery filings with state PUCs, FEMA reimbursement claims, and storm cost deferral accounting under FASB ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulatory Assets; State PUC Storm Cost Recovery Filings

description: Timestamp of the most recent modification to this cost center master record in the source system. Used for change detection in ETL pipelines, audit trail maintenance, and compliance reporting.
reference: SAP FI/CO Audit Trail; FASB ASC 980

description: Physical location or facility code associated with this cost center (e.g., generation plant site code, substation identifier, district office code). Links cost center to a geographic or facility location for asset management integration and GIS-based cost reporting.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Master (Location); Esri ArcGIS GIS Reference

description: SAP CO lock indicator controlling which types of postings are permitted. 'locked_actual' prevents actual cost postings; 'locked_plan' prevents planning entries; 'locked_all' blocks all postings. Used during period-end close, audits, and cost center decommissioning.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Lock Indicator

description: Overhead allocation rate applied to this cost center, expressed as a percentage or fixed amount per activity unit. Used in SAP CO overhead costing sheets to allocate indirect costs (e.g., administrative overhead, facilities costs) to production orders, maintenance orders, and capital projects.
reference: SAP FI/CO Overhead Costing Sheet; Activity-Based Costing (ABC)

description: Specifies whether the overhead rate is applied as a percentage of direct costs, a fixed monetary amount, or an activity-based rate per unit of activity (e.g., per labor hour, per kWh generated). Determines the overhead calculation method in SAP CO.
reference: SAP FI/CO Overhead Costing Sheet Configuration

description: Code of the parent cost center in the organizational hierarchy, enabling hierarchical cost roll-up reporting. Supports the construction of cost center trees for budget consolidation, OPEX allocation, and management reporting.

Functional classification of this cost center for rate case cost-of-service studies filed with state PUCs or FERC. Determines how costs are allocated across customer classes and rate schedules. Aligns with FERC Uniform System of Accounts functional categories. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: generation|transmission|distribution|gas_distribution|customer_service|administrative|common — promote to reference product]
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC General Rate Case (GRC) Requirements; FERC Form 1

description: Abbreviated name of the cost center used in SAP CO reports, budget line items, and dashboard displays where space is constrained. Typically up to 20 characters per SAP standard.

Identifier of the operational source system from which this cost center record was ingested (e.g., 'SAP_CO_PROD', 'SAP_CO_QA'). Supports data lineage, multi-system reconciliation, and Silver Layer provenance tracking in the Databricks Lakehouse.
reference: Enterprise Data Governance Policy; NIST Smart Grid Framework

description: Identifies whether this cost center belongs to the electric utility segment, gas utility segment, common/shared services, or other. Critical for regulatory cost separation, rate case cost-of-service studies, and FERC jurisdictional reporting. Drives allocation of shared costs between electric and gas rate bases.
reference: FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Case Requirements; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP Work Center code linked to this cost center for activity-based costing. Work centers define the capacity and activity rates used to allocate labor and equipment costs to maintenance orders, production orders, and internal orders. Critical for O&M cost tracking.
reference: SAP PM/PP Work Center; Activity-Based Costing (ABC)

description: The date from which this cost center is valid and open for financial postings in SAP CO. Defines the start of the cost center's active period. Used to enforce time-dependent master data validity and support historical cost reporting.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Time-Dependent Master Data

description: The date until which this cost center is valid for financial postings in SAP CO. A far-future date (e.g., 9999-12-31) indicates an open-ended cost center. When set to a past date, the cost center is effectively closed for new postings.
reference: SAP FI/CO Cost Center Time-Dependent Master Data

description: Unique surrogate identifier for the SAP CO internal order record in the Databricks Silver Layer. Primary key for this data product.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Object

description: Surrogate reference to the primary fixed asset or infrastructure asset associated with this internal order. Used when the order collects maintenance or capital costs attributable to a specific T&D asset, generation unit, or facility tracked in the asset management system.
reference: SAP FI-AA Module — Asset Master; Maximo EAM; ISO 55000 Asset Management; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Surrogate reference to the primary fixed asset or infrastructure asset associated with this internal order. Used when the order collects maintenance or capital costs attributable to a specific T&D asset, generation unit, or facility tracked in the asset management system.
reference: SAP FI-AA Module — Asset Master; Maximo EAM; ISO 55000 Asset Management; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Surrogate reference to the SAP CO cost center responsible for this internal order. The responsible cost center is the organizational unit accountable for the costs collected on the order and is used for overhead allocation, budget ownership, and regulatory cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data (Responsible Cost Center); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Surrogate reference to the primary General Ledger account associated with this internal order for cost posting and settlement. Supports chart of accounts alignment and FERC Uniform System of Accounts mapping for regulatory financial reporting.
reference: SAP FI Module — Chart of Accounts; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FASB ASC 980

description: Surrogate reference to the SAP plant (Werk) associated with this internal order, representing the operational facility, service territory, or generation site where the work is performed. Used for geographic cost allocation and asset-level regulatory reporting.
reference: SAP PM/MM Module — Plant Configuration; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Surrogate reference to the SAP PS Work Breakdown Structure (WBS) element to which this internal order is subordinate, when the order is used within a larger capital project structure. Applicable for CAPEX-adjacent overhead orders that support project cost collection.
reference: SAP PS Module — WBS Element; FASB ASC 980 Regulatory Assets; FERC Form 1 CWIP Reporting

description: Total actual costs posted to this internal order to date, in the controlling area currency. Represents the sum of all cost postings (labor, materials, services, overhead) accumulated on the order. Used for OPEX tracking, regulatory cost recovery, and EBITDA reporting.
reference: SAP CO Module — Actual Cost Postings; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Case Filings

description: Total approved budget amount allocated to this internal order for the planning period, in the controlling area currency. Represents the authorized spending limit for the work activity or cost pool. Used for budget availability control and variance analysis in SAP CO.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Budgeting (KO22); FASB ASC 980; State PUC Rate Case Cost Justification

description: SAP CO budget profile (Budgetprofil) assigned to this internal order, defining the rules for budget availability control including tolerance limits, warning thresholds, and error actions when actual or committed costs exceed the approved budget.
reference: SAP CO Module — Budget Profile Configuration (OKO4); Internal Financial Controls

description: SAP FI business area (Geschäftsbereich) associated with this internal order, representing a distinct segment of the utility's operations (e.g., electric generation, electric distribution, gas distribution, corporate). Used for segment-level financial reporting and FERC jurisdictional cost separation.
reference: SAP FI Module — Business Area; FERC Form 1 Jurisdictional Separation; FASB ASC 280

description: The date on which the internal order was fully settled and closed in SAP CO, indicating all costs have been allocated to receivers and the order is archived. Used for financial period-end close management and audit trail.
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Closing (KO88); FASB ASC 980; Financial Audit Requirements

description: Total committed costs on this internal order representing purchase orders and contracts issued but not yet invoiced or posted as actual costs. Used for budget availability control and forecasting remaining spend in SAP CO.
reference: SAP CO Module — Commitment Management; SAP MM Purchase Order Integration

description: SAP FI company code (Buchungskreis) to which this internal order belongs, representing the legal entity or regulated utility subsidiary. Used to segregate costs by legal entity for FERC Form 1, state PUC rate case filings, and consolidated financial reporting.
reference: SAP FI Module — Company Code Configuration; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP CO controlling area (Kostenrechnungskreis) within which this internal order is defined. The controlling area establishes the organizational boundary for management accounting, cost allocation, and internal reporting. Typically maps to a regulated utility entity or holding company segment.
reference: SAP CO Module — Controlling Area Configuration (OKKP)

description: The date and time when this internal order record was first created in SAP CO. Provides the audit trail creation timestamp for data lineage, SOX compliance, and financial record-keeping requirements.
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Creation Timestamp; Sarbanes-Oxley Act (SOX) Section 404; FASB ASC 980

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts on this internal order (budget, planned, actual, committed costs). Typically 'USD' for US-based utility operations. Supports multi-currency controlling area configurations for utilities with international operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP CO Controlling Area Currency; FERC Form 1

description: The planned or actual end date of the internal order, after which no further cost postings are expected. Used for work activity scheduling, budget period closure, and determining when the order should be technically completed and settled.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data (End Date); FERC Form 1 Period Reporting

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USofA) account code associated with the primary cost type collected on this internal order. Enables direct mapping of internal order costs to FERC Form 1 reporting lines for electric and gas utility regulatory filings. Examples: '588' (Maintenance of Overhead Lines), '878' (Gas Transmission and Distribution).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts for Public Utilities and Licensees (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The fiscal year in which this internal order is primarily active and its costs are planned and reported. Used for annual budget cycle management, period-end settlement, and year-over-year cost trend analysis in regulatory rate case filings.
reference: SAP CO Module — Fiscal Year; FERC Form 1 Annual Reporting; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP functional area (Funktionsbereich) assigned to the internal order, used to classify costs by business function for funds management and government/regulatory reporting. Common values in utilities include operations, maintenance, administration, and customer service.
reference: SAP FI/CO Module — Functional Area; FERC Uniform System of Accounts — Functional Classification

description: The date of the most recent period-end settlement run that allocated costs from this internal order to its settlement receivers. Used to confirm that period-end close processes have been completed and to identify orders with outstanding unsettled costs.
reference: SAP CO Module — Settlement Run (KO88/KO8G); FASB ASC 980; Period-End Close Procedures

description: The date and time when this internal order record was most recently modified in SAP CO or the Silver Layer. Used for incremental data pipeline processing, change tracking, and audit trail maintenance.
reference: SAP CO Module — Change Document; SOX Section 404; Databricks Silver Layer Audit Requirements

description: Extended narrative description of the internal order providing full context for the work activity, maintenance job, storm event, or overhead pool. Supports regulatory cost justification in rate case filings and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Long Text; FERC Form 1 Reporting Requirements

description: SAP CO object class (Objektklasse) of the internal order, which determines how costs are treated in profitability analysis and overhead accounting. 'overhead' = indirect cost pool; 'investment' = capital expenditure collection; 'profitability' = revenue-bearing order; 'accrual' = accrual accounting order.
reference: SAP CO Module — Object Class (Field: SCOPE); FASB ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Indicates whether costs collected on this internal order are classified as Operating Expenditure (OPEX), Capital Expenditure (CAPEX), or a mixed allocation. Critical for regulatory cost-of-service studies, rate case filings, and FERC Form 1 reporting. OPEX orders are expensed in the period; CAPEX orders are capitalized to the Regulatory Asset Base (RAB).
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; State PUC Rate Case Guidelines; FASB ASC 360

description: SAP CO internal order category that determines the fundamental accounting treatment. 'overhead_order' = collects overhead costs for allocation to cost centers; 'investment_order' = collects CAPEX costs for capitalization to fixed assets; 'accrual_order' = supports accrual postings; 'order_with_revenues' = collects both costs and revenues for profitability analysis.
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Category (Field: AUTYP); FASB ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The externally-known SAP CO internal order number (Auftragsnummer) assigned by the system at creation. Used as the primary business identifier when referencing the order in financial reports, rate case filings, and cross-system integrations. Typically a numeric string (e.g., '700012345').
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order (KO01/KO02); FERC Form 1 Cost Reporting

description: Current lifecycle status of the SAP CO internal order, reflecting its workflow state. 'created' = order defined but not yet approved for cost collection; 'released' = active and accepting cost postings; 'technically_complete' = operational work done, no further postings allowed but order not yet settled; 'closed' = fully settled and archived; 'deleted' = logically removed.
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Status Management (BS22); FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations

description: SAP CO order type (Auftragsart) that classifies the internal order by its business purpose and controls default parameters such as settlement profile, planning profile, and budget profile. Common utility examples include O&M maintenance orders, storm restoration orders, overhead cost orders, and environmental compliance orders. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: om_maintenance|storm_restoration|overhead_allocation|environmental_compliance|capital_overhead|regulatory_study|safety_compliance — promote to reference product]
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Type Configuration (KOT2); FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Indicates whether this internal order functions as an overhead cost pool for collecting and subsequently allocating indirect costs (e.g., fleet overhead, administrative overhead, safety program costs) to cost centers or other orders via SAP CO overhead allocation cycles.
reference: SAP CO Module — Overhead Cost Controlling; FERC Uniform System of Accounts — Overhead Allocation

description: Total planned (estimated) cost for this internal order as entered in SAP CO cost planning. Represents the expected cost to complete the work activity or fill the overhead pool. Used for budget-to-actual variance analysis and rate case cost-of-service studies.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Planning (KPF6); FERC Form 1 Cost Reporting

description: SAP CO planning profile assigned to this internal order, controlling the cost planning methodology (e.g., overall planning, annual planning, detailed planning by cost element). Used to standardize cost estimation approaches across O&M and overhead orders.
reference: SAP CO Module — Planning Profile Configuration; FERC Form 1 Cost Estimation

description: Surrogate reference to the SAP CO profit center associated with this internal order. Enables profitability analysis by business segment (e.g., electric distribution, gas distribution, generation) and supports segment reporting under FASB ASC 280 and FERC jurisdictional cost separation.
reference: SAP CO Module — Profit Center Accounting (EC-PCA); FASB ASC 280 Segment Reporting; FERC Form 1

description: Indicates whether the costs collected on this internal order are eligible for regulatory cost recovery through rates approved by the PUC or FERC. True = costs are recoverable in rates (e.g., storm restoration, mandated compliance work); False = costs are not recoverable or are subject to disallowance review. Supports regulatory asset/liability accounting under FASB ASC 980.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; State PUC Rate Case Proceedings; FERC Form 1

description: SAP CO cost center code of the organizational unit that requested the creation of this internal order. Distinct from the responsible cost center; used to track which department initiated the work activity or cost collection requirement.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data

description: Name or employee identifier of the person responsible for managing and monitoring this internal order, as recorded in SAP CO master data. Used for cost accountability, budget ownership, and audit trail purposes in financial and regulatory reporting.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data (Responsible Person Field)

description: Type of SAP CO settlement receiver to which costs accumulated on this internal order are settled at period-end. Determines the downstream accounting treatment: 'cost_center' = OPEX allocation; 'fixed_asset' = CAPEX capitalization; 'gl_account' = direct G/L posting; 'wbs_element' = project cost roll-up.
reference: SAP CO Module — Settlement Rule (KO02); FASB ASC 360; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP CO settlement profile (Abrechnungsprofil) assigned to the internal order, defining the rules for how accumulated costs are settled (allocated) to receivers such as cost centers, G/L accounts, fixed assets, or other orders at period-end. Critical for OPEX vs. CAPEX cost classification and regulatory asset capitalization.
reference: SAP CO Module — Settlement Profile Configuration (OKO7); FASB ASC 360 Property Plant and Equipment; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: Brief human-readable description of the internal order's business purpose, as entered in SAP CO (Kurztext field, up to 40 characters). Used in financial reports, cost center allocations, and regulatory filings to identify the nature of the work or cost pool being tracked.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data (KO01)

description: Identifier of the operational source system from which this internal order record was extracted (e.g., 'SAP_CO_PRD' for the SAP CO production client). Supports data lineage tracking and multi-source reconciliation in the Databricks Silver Layer.
reference: Databricks Lakehouse Data Lineage Standards; Enterprise Data Governance Policy

description: The date on which the internal order becomes effective and cost postings are permitted to begin. Represents the planned or actual start of the work activity, maintenance job, or overhead collection period. Used for scheduling, budget period alignment, and regulatory cost period attribution.
reference: SAP CO Module — Internal Order Master Data (Start Date); FERC Form 1 Period Reporting

description: Indicates whether this internal order is a statistical order in SAP CO. True = statistical order used for reporting and analysis purposes only; costs are posted in parallel to a real cost object (cost center or WBS element) and do not affect actual cost flows. False = real order that carries actual costs for settlement.
reference: SAP CO Module — Statistical Internal Orders; FERC Form 1 Supplemental Reporting

description: Indicates whether this internal order was created specifically to capture costs associated with a storm restoration event. True = storm restoration order eligible for separate regulatory cost recovery tracking and potential extraordinary cost treatment. Supports SAIDI/SAIFI reporting and storm cost deferral accounting.
reference: State PUC Storm Cost Recovery Proceedings; FASB ASC 980; NERC Reliability Standards

description: The date on which the internal order was set to 'Technically Complete' status in SAP CO, indicating that the operational work is finished and no further cost postings should occur. Triggers the settlement process and is used for regulatory cost period cut-off in rate case filings.
reference: SAP CO Module — Order Technical Completion (KO02); FERC Form 1 Cost Period Attribution

description: Reference number linking this SAP CO internal order to a corresponding Maximo Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) work order or SAP PM maintenance order. Enables cross-system traceability between financial cost collection and physical asset maintenance activities.
reference: SAP PM Module — Maintenance Order; Maximo EAM Work Order; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each general ledger account record in the chart of accounts. Serves as the primary key for all downstream joins and references across the finance domain.
reference: SAP FI/CO Chart of Accounts; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USoA)

description: High-level financial statement classification of the account indicating its role in the balance sheet or income statement. Values: asset, liability, equity, revenue, expense, other. Drives financial statement presentation and FERC Form 1 schedule mapping.
reference: FASB ASC 980; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USoA) 18 CFR Part 101; GAAP

description: SAP FI/CO account group (field KTOKS) that controls the number range and field status for this GL account. Account groups organize accounts into logical segments (e.g., utility plant, O&M expenses, revenue accounts) for master data governance.
reference: SAP FI/CO T077S Table; FERC Uniform System of Accounts (USoA)

description: Current lifecycle status of the GL account within the chart of accounts. Active accounts accept financial postings; blocked accounts are temporarily restricted; marked_for_deletion accounts are pending archival. Controls posting eligibility in SAP FI/CO.

business_glossary_term: Earnings Before Interest Taxes Depreciation and Amortization (EBITDA) Amount

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Form Number

description: The last calendar date of the reporting period covered by this financial statement (e.g., 2024-12-31 for an annual statement). For balance sheets, this is the as-of date for all reported balances.

description: Total regulatory assets recognized on the balance sheet under FASB ASC 980 rate-regulated accounting. description: The timestamp of the most recent modification to this journal entry line item in SAP FI. Supports change data capture (CDC) for the Databricks Silver Layer ingestion pipeline and SOX Section 404 change audit trail requirements.
reference: SAP FI Module; SOX Section 404; NIST SP 800-92 Log Management

description: The date (AUGDT) on which this open line item was cleared (matched against a payment or offsetting entry) in SAP FI. Null for uncleared items. Used for accounts payable/receivable reconciliation and cash application tracking.

The SAP FI document number (AUGBL) of the clearing transaction that offset this open item. Links payment documents to original invoices or debit memos for accounts payable/receivable reconciliation and audit trail.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 230; FERC Form 1 Audit Requirements

description: The timestamp when this journal entry line item record was first created in the SAP FI system. Provides the audit trail creation timestamp required for SOX Section 404 internal controls and FERC audit documentation.
reference: SAP FI Module; SOX Section 404; FERC Audit Requirements

description: SAP FI debit/credit indicator (SHKZG) specifying whether this line item is a debit (D) or credit (C) posting. Fundamental to double-entry bookkeeping and ensures balanced journal entries for FERC Form 1 and FASB compliance.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 230; FERC Uniform System of Accounts

description: The original document date (BLDAT) of the source business transaction, such as the invoice date or contract date. May differ from the posting date and is used for aging analysis, payment terms, and audit trail documentation.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 450; FERC Form 1

description: SAP FI dunning block indicator (MANSP) that prevents automated dunning (payment reminder) notices for this line item. Used for disputed invoices, regulatory-ordered payment holds, or items under PUC complaint review.
reference: SAP FI Module; State PUC Customer Protection Regulations

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: The FERC Uniform System of Accounts code mapped to this GL line item, used for FERC Form 1 annual report filing. Classifies utility plant, operating revenues, operating expenses, and other accounts per FERC regulatory requirements.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts (18 CFR Part 101); FERC Form 1

description: The SAP fiscal period (MONAT) within the fiscal year, typically 1–12 for monthly periods plus special periods 13–16 for year-end adjustments. Drives monthly financial close and period-over-period variance reporting.
The SAP fiscal year (GJAHR) in which this journal entry line is posted. Used for annual financial close, FERC Form 1 annual reporting, and year-over-year budget variance analysis.
reference: SAP FI Module; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: SAP CO functional area (FKBER) classifying the business function of this posting, such as Generation, Transmission, Distribution, Customer Service, or Administration. Supports cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1 functional classification of expenses.
reference: SAP CO Module; FERC Form 1; GRC Cost-of-Service Study

description: Flag indicating whether this line item represents an intercompany transaction between affiliated entities within the utility holding company structure (True). Required for intercompany elimination in consolidated financial statements and FERC Form 1 affiliated transaction disclosure.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 810 Consolidation; FERC Form 1 Affiliated Transactions

description: Sequential line item number (BUZEI) within the parent journal entry document, ordering debit and credit postings. Ensures the complete audit trail of all line items within a single SAP FI posting document.
reference: SAP FI Module; FERC Form 1 Audit Requirements

description: Current processing status of this journal entry line item in the financial workflow. 'open' indicates an uncleared item; 'cleared' indicates matched/settled; 'parked' indicates a provisional posting pending approval; 'reversed' indicates a correcting reversal; 'in_dispute' indicates a contested amount under review.
reference: SAP FI Module; SOX Section 404; FERC Audit Requirements

description: Free-text description (SGTXT) entered at the line item level in SAP FI, providing narrative context for the posting such as 'Monthly depreciation - Transmission Lines' or 'PPA settlement - Wind Farm Q1'. Supports audit trail and FERC Form 1 explanatory notes.
reference: SAP FI Module; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980

description: The monetary amount of this line item translated into the company code local currency (DMBTR), typically USD for US utility operations. Used for consolidated financial reporting, FERC Form 1, and FASB ASC 980 regulatory accounting.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 830; FERC Form 1

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the company code local currency (HWAER), typically USD. Distinguishes local currency amounts from transaction currency amounts in multi-currency SAP environments.
reference: ISO 4217; SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 830

description: SAP FI payment block indicator (ZLSPR) that prevents automated payment processing for this line item. Used for invoice verification holds, disputed vendor payments, or regulatory compliance holds pending PUC or FERC review.
reference: SAP FI Module; SOX Section 404; FERC Audit Requirements

description: SAP FI payment terms key (ZTERM) applicable to this line item for vendor or customer accounts, defining due dates and early payment discount conditions. Used for cash flow forecasting and accounts payable/receivable management.

SAP logistics plant code (WERKS) associated with this line item, representing a generation facility, service center, or operational location. Links financial postings to physical utility infrastructure for asset accounting and FERC plant account reporting.
reference: SAP MM/PM Module; FERC Form 1 Utility Plant Accounts; ISO 55000 Asset Management

description: The SAP FI posting date (BUDAT) on which this line item is recorded in the General Ledger. Determines the fiscal period assignment and is the primary date for period-end close, FERC Form 1 reporting, and FASB ASC 980 regulatory accounting.
reference: SAP FI Module; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980; FASB ASC 250

description: SAP FI posting key (BSCHL) that determines the debit/credit indicator, account type, and field selection for this line item. Standard values include 40 (GL debit), 50 (GL credit), 01 (customer invoice), 31 (vendor invoice), etc. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: 01|11|21|31|40|50|70|75|80|90 — promote to reference product]

Surrogate identifier referencing the SAP CO profit center associated with this line item. Enables segment-level profitability reporting across business units such as Electric Distribution, Gas Distribution, and Generation.
reference: SAP CO Module; FASB ASC 280 Segment Reporting

description: The quantity (MENGE) associated with this line item, representing physical units such as kWh, MWh, MCF, or Therms for energy commodity postings. Supports energy volume reconciliation between financial postings and operational metering data.
reference: SAP FI/MM Module; EIA Reporting; FERC Form 1

description: External reference document number (XBLNR) from the source transaction, such as a vendor invoice number, purchase order number, or billing document number. Enables cross-system traceability between SAP FI and source systems like Oracle CC&B, Maximo, or Allegro ETRM.
reference: SAP FI Module; FERC Form 1 Audit Trail; SOX Section 404

description: Flag indicating whether this line item relates to a FASB ASC 980 regulatory asset or regulatory liability (True) as approved by a state PUC or FERC rate order. Regulatory assets represent costs deferred for future recovery in customer rates; regulatory liabilities represent obligations to refund customers.
reference: FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations; FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Orders

description: Flag indicating whether this line item is part of a reversal posting (True) or an original posting (False). Reversal postings are used to correct erroneous entries and are required to be disclosed in FERC Form 1 audit trails and SOX Section 404 internal controls documentation.
reference: SAP FI Module; SOX Section 404; FERC Form 1 Audit Trail

description: Amount in the SAP company code second local currency (parallel currency), used for group reporting or regulatory reporting in a secondary currency. Supports consolidated EBITDA and Return on Equity (ROE) calculations at the enterprise level.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 830; SEC Reporting

description: SAP FI special GL indicator (UMSKZ) for down payments, guarantees, bills of exchange, or other special transactions that post to alternative reconciliation accounts. Used for regulatory asset/liability tracking under FASB ASC 980.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 980 Regulatory Assets and Liabilities

description: The tax amount (WMWST) associated with this journal entry line item in transaction currency. Captures sales/use tax, excise tax, or other tax components posted to the GL for regulatory and tax compliance reporting.
reference: SAP FI Module; IRS Tax Code; State PUC Tax Regulations

description: SAP FI tax code (MWSKZ) assigned to this line item, determining the applicable tax rate and tax account determination. Used for sales/use tax compliance, state PUC tax filings, and IRS reporting.
reference: SAP FI Module; IRS Publication 535; State PUC Tax Regulations

description: SAP FI trading partner company code (VBUND) identifying the affiliated entity in intercompany transactions. Required for intercompany elimination in consolidated financial statements and FERC Form 1 intercompany transaction disclosure.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 810 Consolidation; FERC Form 1

description: The monetary amount of this line item in the transaction currency (WRBTR) as posted in SAP FI. Represents the raw debit or credit value before currency translation. Positive value; sign determined by debit_credit_indicator.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency; FERC Form 1

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for the transaction currency (WAERS) of this line item, e.g., USD. Required for multi-currency postings such as Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) settlements or international energy trading transactions.
reference: ISO 4217; SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 830

description: The unit of measure (MEINS) for the quantity field, using SAP internal unit codes. Energy-specific values include KWH (Kilowatt-Hour), MWH (Megawatt-Hour), MCF (Thousand Cubic Feet), and THERM for gas and electric commodity postings. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: KWH|MWH|MCF|THERM|MW|KW|M3|GAL|BBL|EA|HR — 11 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
reference: SAP MM Module; EIA Reporting Standards; FERC Form 1

description: The value date (VALUT) for this line item, representing the date on which the financial transaction takes economic effect for cash management and liquidity planning purposes. Relevant for energy trading settlements and Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) payments.
reference: SAP FI Module; FASB ASC 230 Cash Flow Statements

description: Unique surrogate identifier for each income tax provision record in the lakehouse Silver layer. Primary key for the tax_provision data product.
reference: FASB ASC 740 Income Taxes; SAP FI/CO Tax Ledger

description: Foreign key linking to finance.gl_account. Business justification: Tax Provision references GL Account for tax calculations; FK replaces code.

business_glossary_term: Accumulated Deferred Income Tax (ADIT) Beginning Balance Amount
description: Opening balance of accumulated deferred income taxes (ADIT) for the period. ADIT is a regulatory liability/asset on the rate base that offsets the utility's rate base per PUC orders. Critical for rate case revenue requirement and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 740; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1 Account 190/281/282/283; IRS Normalization Rules IRC §168(i)(9)

business_glossary_term: Accumulated Deferred Income Tax (ADIT) Ending Balance Amount
description: Closing balance of accumulated deferred income taxes (ADIT) for the period after current-period deferred tax expense/benefit and ARAM amortization. Used directly in rate base calculations as a rate base offset per PUC-ordered treatment.
reference: FASB ASC 740; FASB ASC 980; FERC Form 1 Account 190/281/282/283; State PUC Rate Case Orders

description: Name or employee ID of the tax department manager or controller who approved this tax provision record. Required for SOX Section 404 internal control documentation and audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; FASB ASC 740; SAP FI/CO Workflow Approval

description: The date on which the tax provision record received final approval from the authorized approver. Part of the SOX-compliant review and approval workflow for income tax accounting.
reference: SOX Section 302/404; FASB ASC 740; SAP FI/CO Document Approval Date

business_glossary_term: Average Rate Assumption Method (ARAM) Amortization Amount
description: The period amortization of excess ADIT under the Average Rate Assumption Method (ARAM) as required by IRS normalization rules and FERC Order 849. Represents the amount of excess ADIT returned to customers through rate reductions in the current period.
reference: IRS Notice 2018-59; IRC §168(i)(9); FERC Order 849; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) 2017; State PUC TCJA Compliance Orders

description: Additional first-year bonus depreciation claimed under IRC §168(k) for qualifying utility property placed in service during the period. Creates large temporary differences and accelerates ADIT accumulation. Subject to IRS normalization rules for regulated utilities.
reference: IRS IRC §168(k); Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) 2017; IRS Normalization Rules IRC §168(i)(9); FERC Order 849

description: Total GAAP straight-line depreciation for the period as recorded in SAP FI/CO asset accounting. Compared against tax depreciation to compute the accelerated depreciation temporary difference driving the deferred tax liability.
reference: FASB ASC 360; FERC Uniform System of Accounts; SAP FI/CO Asset Accounting (AA)

description: The accounting method used to compute the income tax provision: asset_liability (balance sheet approach per ASC 740), deferred (income statement approach, legacy), or flow_through (used for certain regulatory assets per ASC 980-740). Regulated utilities may use flow-through for specific items per PUC order.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-25; FASB ASC 980-740; State PUC Normalization Orders

description: SAP FI/CO cost center code to which the income tax expense is allocated. Used for segment-level tax expense reporting and rate case cost-of-service allocation by utility function (electric, gas, common).
reference: SAP FI/CO Controlling (CO-CCA); FERC Form 1 Functional Classification

description: The timestamp when this tax provision record was first created in the system. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SOX internal control requirements. Sourced from SAP FI/CO document creation timestamp.
reference: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 740; SAP FI/CO Document Header

description: Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for all monetary amounts in this record (e.g., USD). Supports multi-currency consolidation for entities with foreign operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; FASB ASC 830 Foreign Currency; SAP FI/CO Currency Configuration

description: The portion of total income tax expense attributable to taxes currently payable or refundable for the period. Represents the estimated tax liability on the current-year tax return before deferred items.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; IRS Form 1120; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Taxes

description: Gross deferred tax asset balance representing future tax benefits from deductible temporary differences (e.g., pension obligations, asset retirement obligations, regulatory liabilities). Before valuation allowance offset.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; FERC Form 1 Account 190; SAP FI/CO Deferred Tax Balance Sheet Account

description: The portion of total income tax expense attributable to temporary differences between book and tax basis of assets and liabilities. Positive value indicates deferred tax expense; negative indicates deferred tax benefit.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; FERC Form 1 Schedule of Taxes; IRS Normalization Rules IRC §168(i)(9)

description: Gross deferred tax liability balance representing future tax obligations from taxable temporary differences (e.g., accelerated MACRS depreciation on utility plant, AFUDC equity). Primary driver of ADIT balance for regulated utilities.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; FERC Form 1 Account 281/282/283; IRS MACRS Depreciation; IRC §168

description: The ratio of total income tax expense to pre-tax book income, expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.2100 for 21%). Used in rate case cost-of-service studies and investor reporting. Computed as total_tax_expense_amt / pretax_income_amt.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-50; FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Case Filings

business_glossary_term: Excess Accumulated Deferred Income Tax (Excess ADIT) Amount
description: The excess ADIT balance arising from the reduction in the federal corporate tax rate under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) of 2017. Subject to ARAM (Average Rate Assumption Method) amortization and must be returned to customers per IRS normalization rules and PUC orders.
reference: Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) 2017; IRS Notice 2018-59; IRC §168(i)(9); FERC Order 849; State PUC TCJA Compliance Orders

business_glossary_term: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) Account Code
description: FERC Uniform System of Accounts code associated with this tax provision record (e.g., Account 190 for deferred income taxes — other, Account 281/282/283 for accumulated deferred income taxes). Required for FERC Form 1 annual report filing.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts 18 CFR Part 101; FERC Form 1

description: The accounting period (1–12 for monthly, or 1–4 for quarterly) within the fiscal year to which this provision record applies. Supports interim period tax accounting per FASB ASC 740-270.
reference: FASB ASC 740-270 Interim Reporting; SAP FI/CO Posting Period

description: The fiscal year (e.g., 2024) to which this tax provision record applies. Used for period-over-period comparison, rate case cost-of-service studies, and FERC Form 1 annual reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 740; FERC Form 1; SAP FI/CO Fiscal Year Variant

business_glossary_term: Interest on Uncertain Tax Position (UTP) Amount
description: Accrued interest expense on uncertain tax position reserves. Classified as income tax expense or interest expense per the entity's accounting policy election under ASC 740-10-45-25.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-45-25; IRS IRC §6601 Interest on Underpayments

description: Deferred investment tax credit balance for regulated utilities that defer and amortize ITC over the life of the related asset per the deferral method (FASB ASC 980-740). Distinct from current-period ITC flow-through. Tracked separately for normalization compliance.
reference: FASB ASC 980-740; IRS IRC §48; FERC Form 1 Account 255; IRS Normalization Rules

description: Code identifying the taxing jurisdiction (e.g., US-FED for federal, US-CA for California, US-TX for Texas). Drives apportionment factor application and state/federal tax rate differentiation.
reference: IRS Publication 542; State PUC Filings; FERC Form 1 Tax Schedule

description: Classification of the taxing authority level: federal (IRS), state (state revenue department), local (municipal), or foreign. Determines applicable tax code, rate schedules, and regulatory reporting requirements.
reference: IRS Internal Revenue Code; FASB ASC 740-10; FERC Form 1

description: The timestamp when this tax provision record was most recently modified. Tracks revisions to provision calculations, true-up adjustments, and amended filings. Essential for Silver layer incremental load processing and audit trail.
reference: SOX Section 404; FASB ASC 740; Databricks Delta Lake Change Data Feed

description: Code identifying the legal entity (subsidiary or consolidated parent) for which the tax provision is computed. Aligns with SAP company code structure and FERC Form 1 respondent entity.
reference: SAP FI/CO Company Code; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 740-10-15

description: Cumulative net operating loss carryforward balance available to offset future taxable income. Post-TCJA, federal NOLs are carried forward indefinitely but limited to 80% of taxable income. Generates a deferred tax asset subject to valuation allowance assessment.
reference: IRS IRC §172; Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) 2017; FASB ASC 740-10-30

description: Indicates whether this tax provision record is in compliance with IRS normalization requirements for regulated utilities (IRC §168(i)(9)). Non-compliance can result in loss of accelerated depreciation benefits. Monitored for FERC and PUC regulatory filings.
reference: IRS IRC §168(i)(9); IRS Notice 2018-59; FERC Order 849; State PUC Normalization Orders

business_glossary_term: Penalties on Uncertain Tax Position (UTP) Amount
description: Accrued tax penalties associated with uncertain tax positions. Classified as income tax expense per the entity's accounting policy election. Monitored for rate case disallowance risk.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-45-25; IRS IRC §6662 Accuracy-Related Penalties

description: Net permanent differences between book income and taxable income that never reverse (e.g., tax-exempt interest, non-deductible penalties, AFUDC equity component). Key reconciling item in the effective tax rate reconciliation schedule.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-50-12; IRS Internal Revenue Code; FERC Form 1 ETR Reconciliation

description: Total book income (GAAP) before income tax expense for the period and jurisdiction. Starting point for the effective tax rate reconciliation and current/deferred tax expense computation. Sourced from SAP FI/CO profit center reporting.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; FERC Form 1 Income Statement; SAP FI/CO Profit Center Ledger

description: The business date on which the income tax provision was calculated and recorded. Represents the principal business event date for this transaction record. Typically the last day of the fiscal period.
reference: FASB ASC 740; SAP FI/CO Posting Date

description: Externally-known business identifier for the tax provision record, typically sourced from SAP FI/CO tax calculation run (e.g., TP-2024-FED-Q4). Used for cross-system reconciliation and audit trail.
reference: SAP FI/CO Tax Module; FERC Form 1 Schedule; FASB ASC 740

description: Current lifecycle state of the tax provision record: draft (initial calculation), under_review (tax department review), approved (CFO/controller sign-off), filed (included in tax return), amended (restated), or closed (finalized and archived).
reference: FASB ASC 740; SOX Section 404 Internal Controls; SAP FI/CO Document Status

description: Classifies the nature of the provision calculation: annual (year-end), interim quarterly or monthly (ASC 740-270 estimated annual effective tax rate), true-up (post-filing adjustment), or amended (restated provision). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: annual|interim_quarterly|interim_monthly|true_up|amended — promote to reference product]
reference: FASB ASC 740-270; SAP FI/CO Tax Calculation Run Type

description: The PUC or FERC docket number of the rate case in which this tax provision data is used as supporting evidence for the revenue requirement calculation. Links tax provision to the regulatory proceeding.
reference: State PUC Rate Case Rules; FERC Rate Case Procedures; FASB ASC 980

description: The income tax effect of regulatory liabilities (e.g., excess ADIT returned to customers, over-recovered revenues) recognized under FASB ASC 980. Represents the deferred tax component of regulatory liabilities on the balance sheet.
reference: FASB ASC 980-740; FASB ASC 740; FERC Form 1; State PUC Rate Orders

description: The blended apportionment factor (sales/receipts, payroll, property — weighted per state formula) used to allocate multi-state income to a specific state jurisdiction. Expressed as a decimal (e.g., 0.4523 for 45.23%). Required for state income tax provision calculations.
reference: Multistate Tax Compact; State Revenue Codes; FERC Form 1; Uniform Division of Income for Tax Purposes Act (UDITPA)

description: The enacted statutory income tax rate applicable to the legal entity for the jurisdiction and fiscal year (e.g., 0.2100 for 21% federal corporate rate post-TCJA). Used as the baseline for effective tax rate reconciliation.
reference: IRC §11 (Federal Corporate Tax Rate); Tax Cuts and Jobs Act (TCJA) 2017; State Revenue Codes

description: Total income tax credits recognized in the period, including production tax credits (PTC) for wind/solar generation, investment tax credits (ITC) for renewable energy assets, and R&D credits. Reduces current tax expense dollar-for-dollar.
reference: IRS IRC §45 (PTC); IRS IRC §48 (ITC); Inflation Reduction Act 2022; FASB ASC 740-10; FERC Form 1

description: Total tax depreciation claimed for the period under IRS Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System (MACRS). Typically exceeds book depreciation for utility plant, creating the primary taxable temporary difference and deferred tax liability for regulated utilities.
reference: IRS IRC §168 MACRS; IRS Publication 946; FERC Form 1 Depreciation Schedule

description: Indicates whether the provision is computed on a consolidated federal return, separate company basis, combined state return, or unitary state return. Critical for apportionment factor allocation and intercompany tax sharing agreement calculations.
reference: IRS Reg. 1.1502; State Unitary/Combined Reporting Rules; FASB ASC 740-10-30

description: Net aggregate temporary difference between book and tax basis of assets and liabilities for the period and jurisdiction. Drives the deferred tax expense/benefit calculation. Includes accelerated depreciation, regulatory assets/liabilities, and pension timing differences.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-25; IRS MACRS; FERC Form 1

description: Sum of current and deferred income tax expense for the period. Equals the total provision for income taxes reported on the GAAP income statement. Used in EBITDA reconciliation and rate case revenue requirement calculations.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30; FERC Form 1; FASB ASC 980 Regulated Operations

description: Reserve for uncertain tax positions (UTPs) under the more-likely-than-not recognition threshold. Represents the cumulative liability for tax positions that may not be sustained upon IRS or state examination. Disclosed in financial statement footnotes.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-25 (FIN 48); IRS Schedule UTP; SOX Section 404

description: The regulated utility service type to which this tax provision is attributed: electric, gas, common (shared), water, or steam. Required for functional separation in rate case cost-of-service studies and FERC Form 1 reporting.
reference: FERC Uniform System of Accounts; State PUC Functional Separation Rules; FASB ASC 980

business_glossary_term: Deferred Tax Asset Valuation Allowance Amount
description: Valuation allowance recorded against gross deferred tax assets when it is more likely than not that some portion will not be realized. Reduces net deferred tax asset on the balance sheet per ASC 740 realizability assessment.
reference: FASB ASC 740-10-30-5; SAP FI/CO Valuation Allowance Account
